Several comments:
1. image/video SSL methods differ by whether they use reconstruction or not. Joint embedding architect
title_en:
Several comments:
1. image/video SSL methods differ by whether they use reconstruction or not. Joint embedding architectures Amy or may not have a predictor (JEA vs JEPA). They also differ by their anti-collapse method and data corruption/augmentation methods.
2. DINO *is* a kind of JEPA (technically a JEA). The difference with other JEPA models is the anti-collapse criterion (based on contrative clustering+ stopgradient/EMA), and the data augmentation scheme (image transformations, which is task specific),
3. V-JEPA 2.1, like DINO, is from Meta-FAIR (corporate lab), involved significant engineering teams, large/proprietary datasets, considerable computing resources, lots of fine-tuning, and number-pushing on many benchmarks.
4. Many JEPA papers are applications and/or fine-tuned versions of DINO, V-JEPA or I-JEPA.
5. LeJEPA, LeWM, and most other papers with "JEPA" in the title are *research* papers focused on the methodology, often done by students in academic labs, involving no engineering support, very little computing resources, and small/public training sets. They are generally tested on toy problems, simulated environments, or small/public benchmarks.
6. You simply cannot compare 5 with 2/3/4. 5 gives you ideas and new methods, not models. 2/3 give you well-engineered models, with lots of empirically validated tricks. Only rarely will 2/3 give you a new, well-principled method with room to spare. 5 give you empirical results on new applications.
7. What is published in 5 are methods that will eventually become like 2 and 3, whenever someone with resources picks it up and scales it.

DO NOT CONFUSE UPSTREAM FOUNDATIONAL RESEARCH ON METHODS AND DOWNSTREAM SCALING -> ENGINEERING -> NUMBER PUSHING -> MODELS -> PRODUCTS.
The former makes the rest possible, but it takes time.
title_zh:
几点评论：
1. 图像/视频 SSL 方法因是否使用重建而有所不同。联合嵌入架构 Amy 或可能没有预测器（JEA 与 JEPA）。它们的防崩溃方法和数据损坏/增强方法也有所不同。
2. DINO *是*一种 JEPA（技术上是 JEA）。

Several comments:
1. image/video SSL methods differ by whether they use reconstruction or not. Joint embedding architectures Amy or may not have a predictor (JEA vs JEPA). They also differ by their anti-collapse method and data corruption/augmentation methods.
2. DINO *is* a kind of JEPA (technically a JEA). The difference with other JEPA models is the anti-collapse criterion (based on contrative clustering+ stopgradient/EMA), and the data augmentation scheme (image transformations, which is task specific),
3. V-JEPA 2.1, like DINO, is from Meta-FAIR (corporate lab), involved significant engineering teams, large/proprietary datasets, considerable computing resources, lots of fine-tuning, and number-pushing on many benchmarks.
4. Many JEPA papers are applications and/or fine-tuned versions of DINO, V-JEPA or I-JEPA.
5. LeJEPA, LeWM, and most other papers with "JEPA" in the title are *research* papers focused on the methodology, often done by students in academic labs, involving no engineering support, very little computing resources, and small/public training sets. They are generally tested on toy problems, simulated environments, or small/public benchmarks.
6. You simply cannot compare 5 with 2/3/4. 5 gives you ideas and new methods, not models. 2/3 give you well-engineered models, with lots of empirically validated tricks. Only rarely will 2/3 give you a new, well-principled method with room to spare. 5 give you empirical results on new applications.
7. What is published in 5 are methods that will eventually become like 2 and 3, whenever someone with resources picks it up and scales it.

DO NOT CONFUSE UPSTREAM FOUNDATIONAL RESEARCH ON METHODS AND DOWNSTREAM SCALING -> ENGINEERING -> NUMBER PUSHING -> MODELS -> PRODUCTS.
The former makes the rest possible, but it takes time.
full_text_zh:
几点评论：
1. 图像/视频 SSL 方法因是否使用重建而有所不同。联合嵌入架构 Amy 或可能没有预测器（JEA 与 JEPA）。它们的防崩溃方法和数据损坏/增强方法也有所不同。
2. DINO *是*一种 JEPA（技术上是 JEA）。与其他JEPA模型的区别在于抗崩溃准则（基于对比聚类+ stopgradient / EMA），以及数据增强方案（图像变换，这是特定于任务的），
3. V-JEPA 2.1 与 DINO 一样，来自 Meta-FAIR（企业实验室），涉及重要的工程团队、大型/专有数据集、大量计算资源、大量微调以及许多基准上的数字推送。
4. 许多 JEPA 论文是 DINO、V-JEPA 或 I-JEPA 的应用程序和/或微调版本。
5. LeJEPA、LeWM 和大多数其他标题中带有“JEPA”的论文都是专注于方法论的“研究”论文，通常由学生在学术实验室中完成，不涉及工程支持、很少的计算资源和小型/公共训练集。它们通常在玩具问题、模拟环境或小型/公共基准测试上进行测试。
6. 你根本无法将 5 与 2/3/4 进行比较。 5 给你的是想法和新方法，而不是模型。 2/3 为您提供精心设计的模型，其中包含许多经过经验验证的技巧。只有极少数情况下，2/3 的人才会为您提供一种新的、原则性良好且有余地的方法。 5 为您提供新应用的实证结果。
7. 5 中发布的方法最终将变得像 2 和 3 一样，只要有资源的人拿起它并扩展它。

不要混淆上游方法的基础研究和下游扩展 -> 工程 -> 数字推送 -> 模型 -> 产品。
前者使其余的成为可能，但这需要时间。

title:
Anthropic engineer Addy Osmani warns that AI could make us stop thinking for ourselves.

Working on Claude Code, he says
title_en:
Anthropic engineer Addy Osmani warns that AI could make us stop thinking for ourselves.

Working on Claude Code, he says AI agents now handle so much of his work that he rarely needs to use critical thinking.

He identifies three stages: “cognitive offloading” (delegating tasks), “deferral” (accepting AI answers) and “cognitive surrender” (trusting AI completely).

“Skills that you stop exercising are going to go away, and probably faster than you might guess.”

title_en:
Yes. They use AI to generate votes from fictitious polling units, add to real polling units and come to announce in collation centre that they have results from X, Y, Z polling units. 

Example for the intellectually challenged. 

We have 5 polling units in your street. All 5 polling units vote for say NDC and votes are 500 votes from those polling units, right? 

INEC will say “Oh there are really 9 polling units on that street”. No one can verify the other additional 4 polling units. No one is voting there as it’s all fake. 

Time to collate and they bring out results for 9 polling units with their pumped results. 

Nobody actually checks each polling units. All we see on TV during collation are LG results really. 

One LG equals about 100-200 polling units. If they do that pattern for the APC, they will always win every LG with that pattern. 

I made a tweet this morning about polling unit agents. It’s also captured there. 

Eunice has been screaming this but it’s time to take it seriously.

title: SpaceX and Tesla have prospered in Texas, because we were not constantly operating under an oppressive and extractive st
title_en:
SpaceX and Tesla have prospered in Texas, because we were not constantly operating under an oppressive and extractive state government. 

And I need to be close to the factories, so that I can walk the floor in person. That’s why the first major SpaceX factory was in LA and first major Tesla factory was in SF Bay Area.

As California became increasingly difficult, due to extreme taxes and overregulation, we moved our major domestic expansions and HQ to Texas.
title_zh:
SpaceX 和特斯拉在德克萨斯州蓬勃发展，因为我们并没有一直在一个压迫性和榨取性的州政府下运营。

而且我需要靠近工厂，这样我才能亲自到工厂走一走。这就是为什么 SpaceX 的第一家大型工厂位于洛杉矶，特斯拉的第一家大型工厂位于旧金山

title: Claude Code can design furniture part by part and then give you a bill of materials to order each part and put it togeth
title_en:
Claude Code can design furniture part by part and then give you a bill of materials to order each part and put it together yourself 

And way cheaper than big interior brands sell you their furniture

Furnishing my house I discovered how absolutely insane prices are for the most basic cheap materials put together with a fancy brand tied to it

One shop had a sofa for $30,000 😂

I think with Opus 5.5 and other models easily operating 3d programs like Blender and FreeCAD (both free) it makes more sense to cut out the middle man and go straight to suppliers and design and build your own furniture

Which in a way makes customers more powerful (they can get exactly what they want and usually for cheaper without the markup)

Anyway @theannalux designed this table from scratch, she's not a furniture designer, not a coder, she just had an idea of a style and worked with Claude Code in the terminal (far superior to the app I will keep saying this)

If you design your own furniture and buy the raw materials directly, you can save 85% compared to premium brands like Poliform

That means the $30,000 sofa becomes $4,500! And the $8,000 dinner table becomes just $1,200!

You can see where the idea comes from that AI will make everything 5x to 20x cheaper, and it's already starting!

title:
I've changed how I work over the last few weeks.

I now have one lead agent for each area of focus, running all the time
title_en:
I've changed how I work over the last few weeks.

I now have one lead agent for each area of focus, running all the time, and a chief of staff agent that oversees them. Each lead manages its own sub-agents that write code, test it, chase reviews, and coordinate with team members.

Everything I need to decide or review comes into one prioritized queue, a simple local web app. Each product review includes screenshots and a video demo of the feature. I clear the queue in batches, mostly by voice and keyboard shortcuts. The leads also bring back ideas I hadn't considered.

Working from one queue, instead of switching between dozens of chats, has cut a lot of mental overhead. The system keeps learning my preferences and distilling my judgment into a "Brian brain," so its recommendations and first drafts get better before they reach me. The goal is fewer corrections per change.

Every change still goes through the same human review and security checks. It is eliminating tasks, not human judgment.

What an exciting time to push the frontier of productivity, especially as we build the economy for agents (agentic finance). We should all keep pushing in this direction.

title: This sounds extreme and I wouldn’t have believed it even a year ago, but we’re starting to see plenty of examples of pro
title_en:
This sounds extreme and I wouldn’t have believed it even a year ago, but we’re starting to see plenty of examples of productivity gains that are an order of magnitude or two above output levels pre-AI. 

With the right harness, a deep understanding of your domain of what you want to build, likely a relatively new codebase (with some exceptions), a fluency of how to work with multiple agents at once, and a setup that makes it so you can test and deploy with limited friction, outputs on this level feel realistic in coding.  

What’s crazy is this gap doesn’t appear to be diminishing over time. You’d think that we’d see a convergence in the lines because of AI, but it turns out the more depth you had before -and willingness now to take a different approach- gives you crazy leverage. And that is only compounding as the models can take on larger work and harder problems.

Right now this is most pronounced in software engineering for the obvious reasons. But there’s no reason we don’t start to see this in a number of other computer-use-sensitive domains like other scientific fields, AEC, finance, cyber, and more. Going to get quite wild.

With the right harness, a deep understanding of your domain of what you want to build, likely a relatively new codebase (with some exceptions), a fluency of how to work with multiple agents at once, and a setup that makes it so you can test and deploy with limited friction, outputs on this level feel realistic in coding.  

What’s crazy is this gap doesn’t appear to be diminishing over time. You’d think that we’d see a convergence in the lines because of AI, but it turns out the more depth you had before -and willingness now to take a different approach- gives you crazy leverage. And that is only compounding as the models can take on larger work and harder problems.

full_text_zh:
这听起来很极端，即使在一年前我也不会相信，但我们开始看到大量生产率提高的例子，这些生产率提高比人工智能出现之前的产出水平高一个或两个数量级。

有了正确的工具、对您想要构建的领域的深入了解、可能是一个相对较新的代码库（有一些例外）、如何流畅地同时与多个代理一起工作，以及一个使您可以在有限的摩擦下进行测试和部署的设置，这个级别的输出在编码中感觉很现实。

疯狂的是，这种差距似乎并没有随着时间的推移而缩小。你可能会认为，由于人工智能，我们会看到线条的融合，但事实证明，你之前拥有的深度——以及现在采取不同方法的意愿——给你带来了疯狂的影响力。随着模型可以承担更大的工作和更困难的问题，这种情况只会变得更加复杂。

目前，由于显而易见的原因，这种情况在软件工程中最为明显。但我们没有理由不开始在许多其他计算机使用敏感领域（例如其他科学领域、AEC、金融、网络等）看到这一点。会变得非常狂野。

title:

A creator reportedly used Claude Code to investigate his Andro
title_en:
🚨 YOUR ANDROID PHONE MAY BE STORING MORE THAN YOU THINK.

A creator reportedly used Claude Code to investigate his Android device and discovered over 14,219 images in hidden system directories.

The shocking part? Some appeared to be captured by the front camera.

Here’s what he reportedly found:

→ Images stored outside the normal gallery
→ Face Unlock and system-related cache files
→ Thousands of regular and infrared images
→ Files potentially containing timestamps and location metadata

How did he uncover them?

He connected his Android phone to a computer and used Claude Code to investigate hidden directories.

The discovery raises serious questions about how facial recognition systems process and store biometric data.

⚠️ Important: Hidden image files don’t automatically mean someone is spying on you. Some may be temporary facial recognition data, diagnostic files, or cached images. This claim also hasn’t been independently verified.

Still, it’s a reminder to review your camera permissions, privacy settings, and device storage.

AI isn’t just helping us build things anymore.

It’s helping us investigate what our devices might be hiding.

Would you trust your phone’s facial recognition after seeing this? 👀

Save this post for your next Android privacy check.

full_text_zh:
🚨 您的 Android 手机存储的数据可能比您想象的还要多。

据报道，一名创作者使用 Claude Code 来调查他的 Android 设备，并在隐藏的系统目录中发现了超过 14,219 张图像。

令人震惊的部分？有些似乎是由前置摄像头捕捉到的。

据报道，这是他的发现：

→ 存储在普通图库之外的图像
→ 人脸解锁和系统相关的缓存文件
→ 数千张常规图像和红外图像
→ 可能包含时间戳和位置元数据的文件

他是如何发现它们的？

他将 Android 手机连接到计算机，并使用 Claude Code 来调查隐藏目录。

这一发现引发了关于面部识别系统如何处理和存储生物识别数据的严重问题。

⚠️重要提示：隐藏图像文件并不自动意味着有人在监视您。有些可能是临时面部识别数据、诊断文件或缓存图像。这一说法也尚未得到独立证实。

尽管如此，还是提醒您检查您的相机权限、隐私设置和设备存储。

人工智能不再只是帮助我们建造东西。

它帮助我们调查我们的设备可能隐藏了什么。

看到这个之后你会相信你手机的面部识别吗？ 👀

title_en:
$PLTR Palantir Stock Investors Just Got Great News From a Wall Street Analyst 
(Hint: The Stock Could Soar) 🚀📈🔮
JPMorgan Chase analyst Brian Essex believes Palantir is deeply undervalued: “Palantir’s strategy is to build and offer a platform that can accommodate the world’s most difficult and highest-return AI use cases.” 🎯👊🏻💥

Nov 7, 2026
Key Points
🔹JPMorgan Chase analyst Brian Essex recently initiated coverage of Palantir; his target price of $262 per share is one of the highest on Wall Street.

🔹Palantir is a leader in artificial intelligence platforms, and its ontology-based software arguably gives it a durable competitive advantage.

🔹Palantir is the most expensive stock in the S&P 500 in terms of its price-to-sales ratio, but Essex says the valuation is justified by rapid revenue growth.

Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ: PLTR) has been one of the biggest winners of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, in both share price appreciation and business expansion. The stock has added 2,400% since ChatGPT popularized generative AI in January 2023, and revenue growth has accelerated in 13 consecutive quarters.

Palantir investors recently got great news. In late October, JPMorgan Chase analyst Brian Essex initiated coverage of the company, awarding Palantir a buy rating and a target price of $262 per share. That is one of the most bullish forecasts on Wall Street and it implies 63% upside from the current share price of $160. 🚀

Here’s what investors need to know.

Palantir is a recognized leader in artificial intelligence platforms ✔️

Palantir develops analytics platforms that help government and commercial customers integrate and make sense of complex data. The company supplements its core analytics products with an integrated artificial intelligence (AI) platform called AIP, which serves as a large language model orchestration tool that lets clients swap models without rewriting applications, while retaining control over their sensitive data.

Brian Essex at JPMorgan Chase argues that Palantir has a durable economic moat in its ontology-based software. An ontology unifies data from disparate systems into critical workflows, helping clients make better decisions and automate business processes. For example, Palantir can help manufacturers navigate supplier delays by identifying which customer orders are at risk and deciding how to reallocate inventory.

Forrester Research recently recognized Palantir as a leader in AI platforms. In terms of current capabilities, the analysts ranked its platform above products from all competitors except C3. ai, but the report distinguished Palantir as having the stronger growth strategy. “Palantir’s strategy is to build and offer a platform that can accommodate the world’s most difficult and highest-return AI use cases.” 🔥

Palantir’s revenue growth has now accelerated in 13 straight quarters

JPMorgan Chase analyst Brian Essex justified his target price in a recent note. “As we move from a year where enterprises are just figuring out how to deploy the most transformational technology we have seen in our lifetime to one where they are looking for return, Palantir is already delivering ROI by leveraging its platform to fundamentally transform the business operations of its customers, and growth is accelerating.” 👊🏻

Indeed, Palantir has consistently delivered impressive financial results. In the third quarter, revenue increased 96% to $2.3 billion, marking the 13th straight acceleration. That strong top-line growth was driven largely by momentum in the U.S. commercial business, where sales increased 119%. Meanwhile, non-GAAP earnings soared 144% to $0.44 per diluted share.

In his shareholder letter, CEO Alex Karp wrote, “We have now essentially doubled our entire business since the same quarter last year.” And he expects that strength to persist for the foreseeable future. Palantir raised its full-year guidance, with sales now forecast to climb 156% to $8.5 billion in 2026, a significant acceleration from the 75% sales growth reported in 2025. 🦄

JPMorgan’s Brian Essex is not concerned by Palantir’s expensive valuation 🎯

For many investors, Palantir’s rich valuation punches a hole in the investment thesis. Yes, the company has emerged as the standard in enterprise AI, and its business is growing at a phenomenal pace. But the current valuation of 53 times sales makes it the most expensive stock in the S&P 500, with Moderna ranking second at 47 times sales.

Is the business growing quickly enough to justify that valuation multiple? Brian Essex at JPMorgan says the answer is yes. “Valuation is reasonable when taking into account the company’s uniquely profitable hyper-growth fundamentals, with potential for substantial disruptive upside within its primary market segments,” he wrote in a note to clients.

Many Wall Street analysts agree with Essex and think the stock is undervalued at its current price. In fact, among 38 analysts who follow the company, Palantir has a median target price of $235 per share. That implies 46% upside from the current share price of $160.
By Trevor Jennewine, The Motley Fool

$PLTR Palantir 股票投资者刚刚从华尔街分析师那里得到了好消息
（提示：股票可能会飙升）🚀📈🔮
摩根大通分析师 Brian Essex 认为 Palantir 的价值被严重低估：“Palantir 的战略是构建并提供一个能够适应世界上最困难和回报最高的人工智能用例的平台。” 🎯👊🏻💥

2026 年 11 月 7 日
要点
🔹摩根大通分析师 Brian Essex 最近开始对 Palantir 进行报道；他的目标价为每股 262 美元，是华尔街最高的目标价之一。

🔹Palantir 是人工智能平台的领导者，其基于本体的软件可以说赋予其持久的竞争优势。

🔹就市销率而言，Palantir 是标准普尔 500 指数中最昂贵的股票，但 Essex 表示，收入的快速增长证明了估值的合理性。

Palantir Technologies（纳斯达克股票代码：PLTR）无论在股价升值还是业务扩张方面，都是人工智能（AI）热潮的最大赢家之一。自2023年1月ChatGPT普及生成式人工智能以来，该股已上涨2,400%，收入连续13个季度加速增长。

Palantir 投资者最近得到了好消息。 10 月下旬，摩根大通分析师 Brian Essex 开始对该公司进行报道，给予 Palantir 买入评级和每股 262 美元的目标价。这是华尔街最乐观的预测之一，意味着该股较当前 160 美元的股价上涨 63%。 🚀

这是投资者需要了解的内容。

Palantir 是人工智能平台领域公认的领导者✔️

Palantir 开发的分析平台可帮助政府和商业客户集成并理解复杂的数据。该公司通过名为 AIP 的集成人工智能 (AI) 平台对其核心分析产品进行了补充，该平台作为大型语言模型编排工具，允许客户在不重写应用程序的情况下交换模型，同时保留对其敏感数据的控制。

摩根大通的布莱恩·埃塞克斯 (Brian Essex) 认为，Palantir 在其基于本体的软件中拥有持久的经济护城河。本体将来自不同系统的数据统一到关键工作流程中，帮助客户做出更好的决策并实现业务流程自动化。例如，Palantir 可以通过识别哪些客户订单存在风险并决定如何重新分配库存来帮助制造商解决供应商延误问题。

Forrester Research 最近将 Palantir 认定为人工智能平台的领导者。就目前的功能而言，分析师将其平台排在除 C3 之外的所有竞争对手的产品之上。 ai，但该报告指出 Palantir 拥有更强大的增长战略。 “Palantir 的战略是构建并提供一个能够适应世界上最困难和回报最高的人工智能用例的平台。” 🔥

Palantir 的收入增长现已连续 13 个季度加速

摩根大通分析师布莱恩·埃塞克斯在最近的一份报告中证明了他的目标价是合理的。 “当我们从企业刚刚弄清楚如何部署我们一生中见过的最具变革性的技术的一年转向寻求回报的一年时，Palantir 已经通过利用其平台从根本上改变客户的业务运营来提供投资回报，并且增长正在加速。” 👊🏻

事实上，Palantir 一直取得令人印象深刻的财务业绩。第三季度收入增长 96%，达到 23 亿美元，连续第 13 个季度增长。收入的强劲增长主要是由美国商业业务的势头推动的，该业务的销售额增长了 119%。与此同时，非 GAAP 收益飙升 144% 至稀释后每股 0.44 美元。

首席执行官亚历克斯·卡普（Alex Karp）在致股东的信中写道：“自去年同一季度以来，我们的整体业务基本上翻了一番。”他预计这种力量在可预见的未来将持续存在。 Palantir 上调了全年指引，目前预计 2026 年销售额将增长 156%，达到 85 亿美元，比 2025 年报告的 75% 销售额增长显着加速。🦄

摩根大通的 Brian Essex 并不担心 Palantir 昂贵的估值 🎯

对于许多投资者来说，Palantir 的高估值在投资论点上留下了漏洞。是的，该公司已经成为企业人工智能的标准，并且其业务正在以惊人的速度增长。但目前53倍销售额的估值使其成为标准普尔500指数中最昂贵的股票，Moderna以47倍销售额排名第二。

该业务的增长速度是否足以证明该估值倍数是合理的？摩根大通的布莱恩·埃塞克斯 (Brian Essex) 表示答案是肯定的。他在给客户的一份报告中写道：“考虑到该公司独特的盈利高速增长基本面，以及在其主要细分市场内具有巨大颠覆性上涨潜力的潜力，估值是合理的。”

title: The shift in Congress and the Senate changes the political landscape in Washington, but it doesn't change the actual law
title_en:
The shift in Congress and the Senate changes the political landscape in Washington, but it doesn't change the actual laws on the books or the daily realities inside an ICE field office. 

With Democrats taking control of both chambers, the immediate focus from commentators is going to be on massive legislative battles or policy stalemates. But anyone who has actually run field operations knows that Congress has two main levers that dictate enforcement: appropriations and oversight. 

First is the money. A new majority can try to squeeze funding for detention beds, transportation logistics, and personnel. When you cut bed space or pull resources from the field, you don't stop the flow you just force local offices to manage a logistical nightmare. If the goal becomes defunding the operational mechanics of enforcement rather than fixing the statutory loopholes, the border crisis just moves further inland into processing backlogs. 

Second is oversight. Expect a wave of hearings targeting DHS operational decisions, enforcement protocols, and data transparency. But there is a massive gap between a congressional committee room and a field agent executing a warrant in NYC. Congress can demand reports all day long, but until they realize that field offices are bound by federal statutory mandates that require real resources to execute, the hearings are just noise.

The baseline of immigration enforcement is governed by the Immigration and Nationality Acy . No matter who holds the gavel in the House or the Senate, those statutory mandates remain. The real test over the next two years isn't the rhetoric coming out of the new committee chairs it's whether the budget actually provides the tools required to enforce the law, or if it intentionally starves the frontline infrastructure.  @Phase2Deport #Immigrationenforcement @ICEgov @DHSgov @DHSGenCounsel

full_text_zh:
国会和参议院的转变改变了华盛顿的政治格局，但它并没有改变书本上的实际法律或 ICE 办事处的日常现实。

随着民主党控制参众两院，评论员的直接关注焦点将是大规模的立法斗争或政策僵局。但任何实际进行过实地行动的人都知道，国会有两个主要的杠杆来决定执法：拨款和监督。

首先是钱。新的多数派可以尝试压缩拘留床位、运输后勤和人员的资金。当你削减床位或从现场调动资源时，你并没有停止流动，只是迫使当地办事处应对后勤噩梦。如果目标是取消执法运作机制的资金，而不是修复法定漏洞，那么边境危机只会进一步向内陆蔓延，导致处理积压案件。

二是监督。预计将出现一波针对国土安全部运营决策、执行协议和数据透明度的听证会。但国会委员会会议室和在纽约执行逮捕令的现场特工之间存在巨大差距。国会可以整天要求报告，但直到他们意识到外地办事处受到联邦法定命令的约束，而这些命令需要真正的资源来执行时，听证会只是噪音。

移民执法的基准由移民和国籍局管辖。无论谁在众议院或参议院掌权，这些法定授权仍然存在。未来两年的真正考验不是新委员会主席的言论，而是预算是否真正提供了执法所需的工具，或者是否故意让一线基础设施陷入饥饿。 @Phase2Deport #Immigrationenforcement @ICEgov @DHSgov @DHSGenCounsel

二是监督。预计将出现一波针对国土安全部运营决策、执行协议和数据透明度的听证会。但国会委员会会议室和在纽约执行逮捕令的现场特工之间存在巨大差距。国会可以整天要求报告，但直到他们意识到外地办事处受到联邦法定命令的约束，而这些命令需要真正的资源来执行时，听证会只是噪音。

移民执法的基准由移民和国籍局管辖。无论谁在众议院或参议院掌权，这些法定授权仍然存在。未来两年的真正考验不是新委员会主席的言论，而是预算是否真正提供了执法所需的工具，或者是否故意让一线基础设施陷入饥饿。 @Phase2Deport #Immigrationenforcement @ICEgov @DHSgov @DHSGenCounsel

The demand for super intelligence is
title_en:
People are confusing political theater and emotion with how the real world works.

The demand for super intelligence is only increasing and we don’t yet have at scale humanoid bots, self driving cars globally, AI in mfg, massive disease discovery , and even close to full AI penetration in business or personal agents scaled which will increase demand maybe millions of times where we are today.

Supply will eventually meet that demand whether it is built in the US, other foreign countries, and in space. The US controls their own destiny. We can choose to be AI sovereign, on the cutting edge, create the most amount of jobs/wealth, and be as secure as possible - making deals that greatly net benefit local communities too. We still have the opportunity to have our cake and eat it too… Or we can fall into a mob driven psyop used as a political wedge to help get one party elected. My gut tells me deals will get made. 

But to be clear, the AI hyperscalers / cloud companies do not need US soil to build AI infrastructure. I think they prefer to have it in the US but these are highly resourced global companies who will go where is needed to fulfill demand. My other guess is the exec branch will start allocating significant amounts of federal land if local communities make themselves a bottleneck. 

If you take one thing away from this post, just know AI infrastructure will get built to meet demand wherever in the world or universe is required. Taking the results of a midterm election in one country (that was mostly expected to be split gov outcome) and applying it to the demand/supply for super intelligence is literally absurd.

对超级智能的需求只会不断增加，而我们还没有大规模的人形机器人、全球范围内的自动驾驶汽车、制造中的人工智能、大规模的疾病发现，甚至还没有接近人工智能在商业或个人代理中的全面渗透，这可能会比今天的需求增加数百万倍。

无论是在美国、其他国家还是在太空中建造，供应最终都会满足这一需求。美国掌握着自己的命运。我们可以选择成为人工智能的主权者，走在最前沿，创造最多的就业机会/财富，并尽可能安全——做出对当地社区也有巨大净利的交易。我们仍然有机会鱼和熊掌兼得……或者我们可能陷入暴徒驱动的心理战，被用作政治楔子，帮助一个政党当选。我的直觉告诉我交易将会达成。

但需要明确的是，人工智能超大规模/云公司不需要美国土壤来建设人工智能基础设施。我认为他们更喜欢在美国开展业务，但这些都是资源丰富的跨国公司，他们会去需要满足需求的地方。我的另一个猜测是，如果当地社区成为瓶颈，执行部门将开始分配大量联邦土地。

如果你从这篇文章中拿走一件事，那就知道人工智能基础设施的建设将满足世界或宇宙中任何需要的地方的需求。将一个国家的中期选举结果（人们普遍认为这会是政府分裂的结果）并将其应用于超级智能的需求/供给实际上是荒谬的。

title: MY BROTHER ASKED ME TO SELL THE HOUSE WE GREW UP IN. I REFUSED UNTIL I FOUND OUT WHAT OUR MOTHER HAD BEEN HIDING FROM BO
title_en:
MY BROTHER ASKED ME TO SELL THE HOUSE WE GREW UP IN. I REFUSED UNTIL I FOUND OUT WHAT OUR MOTHER HAD BEEN HIDING FROM BOTH OF US.

I’m 58 years old, and until last spring, I believed my younger brother and I had one thing left that neither time nor money could take away from us: the house where we grew up.

It wasn’t a mansion. It had three bedrooms, an old wooden staircase that creaked at night, a kitchen window that never closed properly, and a backyard where our mother grew tomatoes every summer.

But it was home.

After our father died, my mother stayed there alone. My brother, Daniel, moved to Colorado. I lived twenty minutes away and visited every Sunday.

I handled her groceries, drove her to appointments, fixed the leaking taps, and sat with her when the evenings became too quiet.

Daniel called every few weeks.

I never complained. We had different lives, and I understood that.

Then, one Tuesday afternoon, Daniel called and said something I wasn’t prepared to hear.

“We need to sell Mom’s house.”

I thought I had misunderstood him.

“Why?”

“Because it’s too much property for one person. Mom can’t live there anymore, and we’re both entitled to our share.”

Our mother was still alive. She had moved into assisted living after a fall, but she was recovering well.

I told him I wasn’t selling anything without her agreement.

He sighed.

“Here we go again. You always act like you’re the only one who cares about her.”

That sentence hurt more than I expected.

I reminded him that I had been the one taking her to physical therapy, arranging repairs, and checking on her every week.

He replied, “I send money.”

I said, “Sending money isn’t the same as showing up.”

He hung up.

For the next few days, we barely spoke.

Then Daniel arrived unexpectedly with a real estate agent.

I was standing in the kitchen when I saw them walking through the living room, measuring the walls and discussing what could be renovated.

I stepped outside.

“What are you doing?”

Daniel looked irritated.

“Just getting an estimate. Nobody is forcing you to sign anything.”

I asked him to leave.

The agent quietly excused himself.

Daniel stayed behind.

“You’re making this difficult for no reason,” he said. “Mom doesn’t need this house anymore.”

I looked at him and replied, “Have you actually asked her what she wants?”

He didn’t answer.

That evening, I visited our mother.

She was sitting beside the window in her room, folding a small blanket she had brought from home.

I told her about Daniel and the real estate agent.

She stopped folding.

For a moment, she looked as though she wanted to say something but couldn’t find the words.

Then she asked, “Did he tell you why he wants to sell it so quickly?”

I said no.

She looked down at her hands.

“Your brother came to see me last month. He asked me to sign some papers.”

“What papers?”

“He said they were needed to make things easier when I was gone.”

I felt my stomach tighten.

“Did you sign them?”

“No.”

She reached into the drawer beside her bed and pulled out a small folder.

Inside were copies of documents, bank statements, and a letter written in her handwriting.

She handed me the letter.

It was dated six months earlier.

I read the first few lines, then looked up at her.

My mother had quietly arranged for the house to be placed in a trust—not to give it to me, not to give it to Daniel, but to protect it from being sold while she was still alive.

There was also a handwritten note explaining why.

She had discovered that Daniel had been struggling financially. He had asked her for money several times, telling her it was for his business.

She had helped him.

But the last time, she learned that he had used the money to cover personal debts and had never told her the truth.

She wasn’t angry that he needed help.

She was hurt that he had lied.

The letter ended with one sentence:

I don’t want either of my children fighting over the only place where we were once happy.

full_text_zh:
我哥哥要我卖掉我们长大的房子。我拒绝了，直到我发现我们的母亲向我们俩隐瞒了什么。

我已经 58 岁了，直到去年春天，我还相信我和弟弟还有一样东西是时间和金钱都无法从我们身边夺走的：我们长大的房子。

这不是一座豪宅。它有三间卧室，一个在晚上吱吱作响的旧木楼梯，一个永远关不严的厨房窗户，还有一个后院，我们的母亲每年夏天都会在那里种植西红柿。

但那是家。

父亲去世后，母亲独自留在那里。我的兄弟丹尼尔搬到了科罗拉多州。我住在离这里二十分钟路程的地方，每周日都会去拜访。

我帮她处理杂货，开车送她去约会，修理漏水的水龙头，当夜晚变得太安静时，我坐在她身边。

丹尼尔每隔几周就会打来电话。

我从不抱怨。我们有不同的生活，我理解这一点。

然后，一个星期二下午，丹尼尔打电话来，说了一些我不准备听的话。

“我们需要卖掉妈妈的房子。”

我以为我误会了他。

“为什么？”

“因为对于一个人来说，这财产太多了。妈妈不能再住在那里了，而我们都有权分得自己的一份。”

我们的母亲还活着。她摔倒后搬进了辅助生活室，但恢复得很好。

我告诉他未经她同意我不会卖任何东西。

他叹了口气。

“又来了。你总是表现得好像你是唯一关心她的人。”

这句话比我预想的更刺痛。

我提醒他，我是带她去物理治疗、安排修理、每周检查她的人。

他回答说：“我寄钱。”

我说：“寄钱和露面不一样。”

他挂断了电话。

接下来的几天，我们几乎没有说话。

然后丹尼尔意外地带着一位房地产经纪人来到了。

当我看到他们穿过客厅、测量墙壁并讨论需要翻新的地方时，我正站在厨房里。

我走出去。

“你在干什么？”

丹尼尔看起来很生气。

“只是得到一个估计。没有人强迫你签署任何东西。”

我请他离开。

经纪人低声告辞。

丹尼尔留在后面。

“你无缘无故地让这件事变得困难，”他说。 “妈妈不再需要这个房子了。”

我看着他：“你真的问过她想要什么吗？”

他没有回答。

那天晚上，我去看望了我们的母亲。

她坐在房间的窗边，叠着从家里带来的小毯子。

我告诉她丹尼尔和房地产经纪人的事。

她停止折叠。

一时之间，她似乎想说什么，却又找不到言语。

然后她问：“他有没有告诉你为什么他要这么快卖掉它？”

我说不。

她低头看着自己的双手。

“你哥哥上个月来看过我。他让我签了一些文件。”

“什么文件？”

“他说当我离开时，他们需要让事情变得更容易。”

我感到胃部发紧。

“你签了字吗？”

“不。”

她把手伸进床边的抽屉里，拿出一个小文件夹。

里面有文件的副本、银行对账单和一封她亲笔写的信。

她把信递给我。

它的日期是六个月前。

我读了前几行，然后抬头看着她。

我母亲悄悄安排把房子交给信托机构——不是把它给我，也不是给丹尼尔，而是为了在她还活着的时候保护它不被出售。

还有一张手写的便条解释了原因。

她发现丹尼尔一直在经济上陷入困境。他曾多次向她要钱，并告诉她这是为了他的生意。

她帮助了他。

但上次，她得知他用这些钱来偿还个人债务，却从未告诉过她真相。

她并不因为他需要帮助而生气。

她因他撒谎而受伤。

这封信以一句话结尾：

我不想让我的两个孩子争夺我们曾经快乐的唯一地方。

上吱吱作响的旧木楼梯，一个永远关不严的厨房窗户，还有一个后院，我们的母亲每年夏天都会在那里种植西红柿。

但那是家。

父亲去世后，母亲独自留在那里。我的兄弟丹尼尔搬到了科罗拉多州。我住在离这里二十分钟路程的地方，每周日都会去拜访。

我帮她处理杂货，开车送她去约会，修理漏水的水龙头，当夜晚变得太安静时，我坐在她身边。

丹尼尔每隔几周就会打来电话。

我从不抱怨。我们有不同的生活，我理解这一点。

然后，一个星期二下午，丹尼尔打电话来，说了一些我不准备听的话。

“我们需要卖掉妈妈的房子。”

我以为我误会了他。

“为什么？”

“因为对于一个人来说，这财产太多了。妈妈不能再住在那里了，而我们都有权分得自己的一份。”

我们的母亲还活着。她摔倒后搬进了辅助生活室，但恢复得很好。

我告诉他未经她同意我不会卖任何东西。

他叹了口气。

“又来了。你总是表现得好像你是唯一关心她的人。”

这句话比我预想的更刺痛。

我提醒他，我是带她去物理治疗、安排修理、每周检查她的人。

他回答说：“我寄钱。”

我说：“寄钱和露面不一样。”

他挂断了电话。

接下来的几天，我们几乎没有说话。

然后丹尼尔意外地带着一位房地产经纪人来到了。

当我看到他们穿过客厅、测量墙壁并讨论需要翻新的地方时，我正站在厨房里。

我走出去。

“你在干什么？”

丹尼尔看起来很生气。

“只是得到一个估计。没有人强迫你签署任何东西。”

我请他离开。

经纪人低声告辞。

丹尼尔留在后面。

“你无缘无故地让这件事变得困难，”他说。 “妈妈不再需要这个房子了。”

我看着他：“你真的问过她想要什么吗？”

他没有回答。

那天晚上，我去看望了我们的母亲。

她坐在房间的窗边，叠着从家里带来的小毯子。

我告诉她丹尼尔和房地产经纪人的事。

她停止折叠。

一时之间，她似乎想说什么，却又找不到言语。

然后她问：“他有没有告诉你为什么他要这么快卖掉它？”

我说不。

她低头看着自己的双手。

“你哥哥上个月来看过我。他让我签了一些文件。”

“什么文件？”

“他说当我离开时，他们需要让事情变得更容易。”

我感到胃部发紧。

“你签了字吗？”

“不。”

她把手伸进床边的抽屉里，拿出一个小文件夹。

Around midnight in Bo
title_en:
ICE Agents Take Down Protesters in Boyle Heights, Then Hold the Line at a Hospital Ambulance Dock

Around midnight in Boyle Heights, Los Angeles, ICE agents in tactical vests rushed down the sidewalk at Boyle Avenue and Pennsylvania Avenue and pinned someone to the ground.  Local reports identify the agents as ICE, and the people taken down as protesters.

About a minute later, agents lead a person away.  When the filmer gets too close, an agent reaches out and shoves them back.

Agents then gather at the trunk of a red car before forming a line across the street with lights flashing.  The filmer claims pepper spray was used, but it isn't seen on camera.

The agents were reportedly in the area waiting for a patient to be released from White Memorial Medical Center, a block away.  Later that night, ICE agents reportedly went in through the hospital's ambulance dock to take someone into custody.

Protesters gathered outside the ambulance entrance, and a tactical line of agents pushed the crowd back.  ICE hasn't released a statement, and no names or charges are out.

The midterms are over, @POTUS why hasn't RINO Mullin given the agents the go ahead to use pepper spray and force to stop the violence of these radicals?  No one should have to work like this.

title_en:
Introducing DECIDE: a benchmark for audio decisions in voice agents, in association with @bolna_dev 

A voice agent doesn’t just transcribe. It decides: speak or wait, route the call, pick a tool, switch language. Text can’t tell you if the caller sounded annoyed, interrupted, or talked over the agent.

DECIDE tests exactly that, on real production calls.

→ 4,867 decision questions from 1,081 real agent-caller clips (3 to 25 seconds)
→ 32 tasks across 6 families: turn-taking, graph routing, tool decisions, language switching, caller emotion, business intent

Direct-audio models and STT + text models (20 in total) are scored on the same questions, so you can see what audio actually adds, and what it costs in dollars and milliseconds.

Submit your model endpoint and get scored; no invite needed.

title: Monica Lewinsky was 22 when she started having sex with the President of the United States. Bill Clinton was 49 and her
title_en:
Monica Lewinsky was 22 when she started having sex with the President of the United States. Bill Clinton was 49 and her boss. She was an unpaid White House intern. They hooked up nine times in the Oval Office. Then her friend from work secretly recorded 20 hours of their phone calls and handed them to the prosecutor. And it was Monica, not the president, whose life was destroyed.

Monica started her internship in July 1995. Four months later she was alone with Clinton for the first time. Their last encounter was in spring 1997. By then she had been moved to a job at the Pentagon.

That's where she met Linda Tripp. Monica told her everything. On the advice of literary agent Lucianne Goldberg, Tripp started recording their calls in secret, which was illegal in Maryland where she lived. And Tripp told Monica not to dry-clean the blue dress with the president's semen on it.

On January 16, 1998, Tripp invited Monica to lunch at the Pentagon City mall food court. She came down the escalator with two FBI agents. They took Monica to room 1012 of the Ritz-Carlton next door. For about 12 hours prosecutors told her she could go to prison for 27 years. She was 24.

Ten days later Clinton went on national TV: "I did not have sexual relations with that woman, Miss Lewinsky."

Monica got immunity and handed the blue dress to Ken Starr. In August the FBI took Clinton's blood for a DNA test. It matched. Clinton admitted the relationship. In December 1998 he was impeached. He stayed in office.

Monica says sympathy lasted "five seconds." After that she was called "a stalker, a whore, mentally unstable, a bimbo."

In 1999, 70 million Americans watched her interview with Barbara Walters. She made $1 million from the international rights and about $500,000 from a book. Jenny Craig signed her for $1 million if she lost 40 pounds. They paid her $300,000.

In 2018 NBC asked Clinton if he owed her an apology. "No, I do not." In 2020 he said he felt "terrible" that the affair had defined her life.

In 2021 Monica produced the TV series about her own scandal, Impeachment: American Crime Story. In 2025 she said Clinton should have resigned instead of throwing a young woman "under the bus." "I lost my future." "I bet nobody has asked Bill if he ever thought about changing his name."

He got impeached and kept his job. She got a blue dress, 27 years on the table and a name she can't change.

Some lessons are written in other people's mistakes. Watch it once. Remember it forever.

在那里她遇到了琳达·特里普。莫妮卡把一切都告诉了她。在文学经纪人卢西安·戈德堡的建议下，特里普开始秘密录音他们的通话，这在她居住的马里兰州是非法的。特里普告诉莫妮卡不要干洗沾有总统精液的蓝色裙子。

1998 年 1 月 16 日，特里普邀请莫妮卡在五角大楼城购物中心美食广场吃午餐。她和两名联邦调查局特工一起走下自动扶梯。他们带着莫妮卡去了隔壁丽思卡尔顿酒店的1012房间。在大约 12 个小时的时间里，检察官告诉她，她可能会入狱 27 年。她24岁。

十天后，克林顿在国家电视台上说道：“我没有与莱温斯基小姐发生性关系。”

莫妮卡获得了豁免权，并将蓝色连衣裙交给了肯·斯塔尔。 8月，联邦调查局抽取了克林顿的血液进行DNA测试。它匹配。克林顿承认了这段关系。 1998年12月，他被弹劾。他留在办公室。

莫妮卡说同情持续了“五秒钟”。此后她被称为“跟踪狂、妓女、精神不稳定、荡妇”。

1999 年，7000 万美国人观看了她对芭芭拉·沃尔特斯 (Barbara Walters) 的采访。她从国际版权中赚了 100 万美元，从一本书中赚了大约 50 万美元。如果她减掉 40 磅，珍妮·克雷格就会以 100 万美元的价格签下她。他们付给她 30 万美元。

2018年，NBC问克林顿是否欠她一个道歉。 “不，我不。” 2020年，他表示，这件事定义了她的生活，他感到“可怕”。

2021 年，莫妮卡制作了有关她自己丑闻的电视剧《弹劾：美国犯罪故事》。 2025 年，她表示克林顿应该辞职，而不是将一名年轻女性“扔到公共汽车底下”。 “我失去了未来。” “我敢打赌没有人问过比尔是否考虑过改名。”

他被弹劾并保住了工作。她穿着蓝色裙子，在赌桌上呆了 27 年，还有一个她无法改变的名字。

有些教训是写在别人的错误中的。看一次。永远记住它。

title:
Jonathan Jones on the 49ers - Brandon Aiyuk situation:

“Multiple sources tell me it will take days, weeks or even month
title_en:
Jonathan Jones on the 49ers - Brandon Aiyuk situation:

“Multiple sources tell me it will take days, weeks or even months for the Brandon Aiyuk saga to reach a conclusion.

That doesn’t mean Aiyuk won’t be eligible to sign with a team as soon as he wants. That well may be the case, if some team is willing to assess and submit to the risk. But there are contractual questions that don’t have a clear answer for either side.

Several factors make the Aiyuk situation unique. He signed a four-year, $120 million contract extension in 2024, played seven games before injury and then went AWOL. Having a signing bonus of $23 million paid out so closely to a player going on the reserve/left squad list doesn’t happen very often. (Even when it happens, that player likely retires — there’s precedent for that.)
If this were cut-and-dried, the 49ers wouldn’t need to be in regular communication with the NFL Management Council and NFL Players Association. As I understand it, the Aiyuk saga falls in a gray area of the collective bargaining agreement.

The 49ers have already voided his guarantees and he never sought them, but will the Niners wind up recouping all $13 million they seek? How ticked off are they? On what principles do the team and new agent Drew Rosenhaus want to stand, and what precedents are they willing to create?

The idea of keeping Aiyuk on the team seems the most absurd given what the head coach and GM have said on the record and what other 49ers players have danced around all week. The second-most absurd idea is a team trading for Aiyuk on his current contract, considering his erratic behavior. A proper franchise would have to conduct real diligence before sending any asset for him.

As one source put it, three major things need to take place if Aiyuk is going to play again this season:

1. He needs to be on his best behavior when meeting with the 49ers. (Check.)
2. The 49ers want to clean their hands of this mess rather quickly. (It appears they do.)
3. He has to be worth it for an acquiring team. That means he must be healthy and trustworthy.

If Aiyuk is on good behavior these next few days/weeks, few would be surprised if he had a workout for a team this season. Teams are always in the market for talented pass catchers, and teams will grant more leniency at this position when it comes to behavior.

To bring him on to a team would create a storyline, though, and he would have to be worth that. An acquiring team surely wouldn’t get good feedback from the Niners. As respected as Rosenhaus is in the NFL, he has been Aiyuk’s agent for less than a week, so how much does he really know about him? And how could a team trust that Aiyuk won’t do something similar as it tries to win the Lombardi Trophy?

To be fair, Aiyuk seems to be coming around. He figuratively lit tens of millions of dollars on fire by not showing up to work, and he’ll likely have to pay back more millions. It was irrational and nonsensical at a basic level. That he has the wherewithal to get back on the right track, after the events of the past year-plus, is commendable.”

full_text_zh:
乔纳森·琼斯谈 49 人队 - 布兰登·艾尤克的情况：

“多个消息来源告诉我，布兰登·艾尤克的传奇故事需要几天、几周甚至几个月的时间才能得出结论。

这并不意味着艾尤克没有资格尽快与球队签约。如果某个团队愿意评估并承担风险，情况可能就是这样。但有些合同问题双方都没有明确的答案。

有几个因素使艾尤克的情况独一无二。他在 2024 年签下了一份为期四年、价值 1.2 亿美元的续约合同，受伤前打了 7 场比赛，然后擅离职守。与预备队/左队名单上的球员如此接近地支付 2300 万美元的签约奖金并不常见。 （即使发生这种情况，该球员也可能会退役——这是有先例的。）
如果这是一成不变的，49人队就不需要与 NFL 管理委员会和 NFL 球员协会定期沟通。据我了解，艾尤克事件属于集体谈判协议的灰色地带。

49 人队已经取消了他的保证，而他也从未寻求过这些保证，但是 9 人队最终会收回他们所寻求的全部 1300 万美元吗？他们有多生气？球队和新经纪人德鲁·罗森豪斯想要坚持什么原则，他们愿意创造什么先例？

考虑到主教练和总经理的记录以及其他 49 人队球员整周的表现，让 Aiyuk 留在球队的想法似乎是最荒谬的。第二个最荒谬的想法是球队根据艾尤克目前的合同交易他，考虑到他不稳定的行为。一个合适的特许经营商在为他发送任何资产之前必须进行真正的尽职调查。

正如一位消息人士所说，如果艾尤克要在本赛季再次上场，需要完成三件事：

1. 在与 49 人队比赛时，他需要表现出最好的表现。 （检查。）
2. 49人队希望尽快清理掉这些烂摊子。 （看来他们确实如此。）
3. 对于收购球队来说，他必须值得。这意味着他必须健康且值得信赖。

如果艾尤克在接下来的几天/几周表现良好，那么如果他本赛季为球队试训，很少有人会感到惊讶。球队总是在市场上寻找有才华的传球接球手，并且在行为方面，球队会给予这个位置更多的宽容。

不过，让他加入一支球队会创造一个故事情节，而且他必须值得这样做。收购球队肯定不会从九人队那里得到好的反馈。尽管罗森豪斯在NFL备受尊敬，但他担任艾尤克的经纪人还不到一周，那么他对艾尤克到底了解多少呢？一支球队怎么能相信 Aiyuk 在试图赢得隆巴尔迪奖杯时不会做类似的事情呢？

公平地说，艾尤克似乎正在回心转意。他因缺勤而烧毁了数千万美元，而且他可能还需要偿还更多数百万美元。从根本上讲，这是不合理和荒谬的。在经历了过去一年多的事件之后，他有足够的资金重回正轨，这是值得赞扬的。”

样。但有些合同问题双方都没有明确的答案。

有几个因素使艾尤克的情况独一无二。他在 2024 年签下了一份为期四年、价值 1.2 亿美元的续约合同，受伤前打了 7 场比赛，然后擅离职守。与预备队/左队名单上的球员如此接近地支付 2300 万美元的签约奖金并不常见。 （即使发生这种情况，该球员也可能会退役——这是有先例的。）
如果这是一成不变的，49人队就不需要与 NFL 管理委员会和 NFL 球员协会定期沟通。据我了解，艾尤克事件属于集体谈判协议的灰色地带。

49 人队已经取消了他的保证，而他也从未寻求过这些保证，但是 9 人队最终会收回他们所寻求的全部 1300 万美元吗？他们有多生气？球队和新经纪人德鲁·罗森豪斯想要坚持什么原则，他们愿意创造什么先例？

考虑到主教练和总经理的记录以及其他 49 人队球员整周的表现，让 Aiyuk 留在球队的想法似乎是最荒谬的。第二个最荒谬的想法是球队根据艾尤克目前的合同交易他，考虑到他不稳定的行为。一个合适的特许经营商在为他发送任何资产之前必须进行真正的尽职调查。

正如一位消息人士所说，如果艾尤克要在本赛季再次上场，需要完成三件事：

1. 在与 49 人队比赛时，他需要表现出最好的表现。 （检查。）
2. 49人队希望尽快清理掉这些烂摊子。 （看来他们确实如此。）
3. 对于收购球队来说，他必须值得。这意味着他必须健康且值得信赖。

如果艾尤克在接下来的几天/几周表现良好，那么如果他本赛季为球队试训，很少有人会感到惊讶。球队总是在市场上寻找有才华的传球接球手，并且在行为方面，球队会给予这个位置更多的宽容。

不过，让他加入一支球队会创造一个故事情节，而且他必须值得这样做。收购球队肯定不会从九人队那里得到好的反馈。尽管罗森豪斯在NFL备受尊敬，但他担任艾尤克的经纪人还不到一周，那么他对艾尤克到底了解多少呢？一支球队怎么能相信 Aiyuk 在试图赢得隆巴尔迪奖杯时不会做类似的事情呢？

公平地说，艾尤克似乎正在回心转意。他因缺勤而烧毁了数千万美元，而且他可能还需要偿还更多数百万美元。从根本上讲，这是不合理和荒谬的。在经历了过去一年多的事件之后，他有足够的资金重回正轨，这是值得赞扬的。”

title: Elon Musk asks every person he interviews for a job at SpaceX or Tesla the same question. The question is not about thei
title_en:
Elon Musk asks every person he interviews for a job at SpaceX or Tesla the same question. The question is not about their resume. It is not about their skills. It is not a brain teaser or a trick question. It is: "Tell me about some of the most difficult problems you worked on and how you solved them." Then he listens. Not to the answer. To the detail.

He has described the logic behind the question in multiple interviews. A person who actually solved a difficult problem can describe it in infinite detail. They remember the blind alleys. They remember the specific moment the solution appeared. They remember which assumption they were wrong about and when they realized it. The description is textured, specific, and non linear because real problem solving is textured, specific, and non linear.

A person who is taking credit for someone else's work cannot describe the detail because they weren't in the room when the detail happened. They describe the problem in general terms. They describe the solution in general terms. They skip the blind alleys because they didn't walk them. They can't name the specific moment the answer appeared because they weren't there when it appeared. The absence of texture is the tell.

Elon has said he can identify fabrication within 60 seconds of the answer beginning. The fabricator gives a clean narrative: problem, approach, solution. The real solver gives a messy narrative: problem, wrong approach, wasted time, revised understanding, new approach, partial solution, refinement, final answer. The mess is the proof. Clean stories are marketing. Messy stories are engineering.

The question also reveals how the candidate thinks, not just what they've done. The person who solved a problem by brute force (trying every option until one worked) thinks differently from the person who solved it by abstraction (identifying the underlying principle and attacking it directly). Both produce solutions. Elon wants the abstractor because the abstractor can transfer the method to new domains. The brute forcer can only apply the method to the original problem.

He has hired people based on a compelling answer to this one question and passed on people with perfect resumes who gave generic answers. The question selects for a specific type of person: someone who has been deep inside a problem, alone, confused, and eventually found the exit. That person, regardless of their degree or their previous employer, is someone who can survive the environment at SpaceX or Tesla where being deep inside a problem, alone, and confused is the default working condition.

The most powerful hiring tool in the most innovative company on earth is one question. Not a coding test. Not a case study. Not a reference check. One question that separates the people who solved the problem from the people who watched someone else solve it. The texture is the proof. The mess is the credential.

full_text_zh:
埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 向他面试 SpaceX 或 Tesla 工作的每一个人提出了同样的问题。问题不在于他们的简历。这与他们的技能无关。这不是一个脑筋急转弯或一个棘手的问题。它是：“告诉我你解决过的一些最困难的问题以及你是如何解决这些问题的。”然后他听着。不给答案。到细节。

他在多次采访中描述了这个问题背后的逻辑。一个真正解决了难题的人可以无限详细地描述它。他们记得死胡同。他们记得解决方案出现的具体时刻。他们记得自己错误的假设是什么以及何时意识到的。描述是有纹理的、具体的和非线性的，因为真正的问题解决是有纹理的、具体的和非线性的。

一个将别人的工作归功于自己的人无法描述细节，因为细节发生时他们并不在房间里。他们笼统地描述了问题。他们笼统地描述了解决方案。他们跳过死胡同，因为他们没有走过死胡同。他们无法说出答案出现的具体时刻，因为答案出现时他们并不在场。缺乏纹理就是说明。

Elon 表示，他可以在回答开始后 60 秒内识别造假行为。制作者给出了清晰的叙述：问题、方法、解决方案。真正的解决者给出了一个混乱的叙述：问题、错误的方法、浪费时间、修改理解、新方法、部分解决、细化、最终答案。混乱就是证据。干净的故事就是营销。混乱的故事是工程。

这个问题还揭示了候选人的想法，而不仅仅是他们做了什么。通过暴力解决问题（尝试每一种选择，直到其中一个可行）的人与通过抽象解决问题（识别基本原理并直接攻击它）的人的思维方式不同。两者都产生解决方案。 Elon 想要抽象器，因为抽象器可以将方法转移到新的域。暴力破解者只能将该方法应用于原始问题。

他根据对这一问题的令人信服的答案来聘用人员，并放弃了简历完美、给出通用答案的人。该问题针对的是特定类型的人：深陷问题之中、孤独、困惑、最终找到出口的人。这个人，无论他们的学位或以前的雇主如何，都是能够在 SpaceX 或 Tesla 的环境中生存下来的人，在这些环境中，深陷问题、孤独和困惑是默认的工作条件。

地球上最具创新精神的公司中最强大的招聘工具是一个问题。不是编码测试。不是案例研究。不是参考检查。这个问题将解决问题的人和看着别人解决问题的人区分开来。质感就是证据。混乱就是凭证。

这个问题还揭示了候选人的想法，而不仅仅是他们做了什么。通过暴力解决问题（尝试每一种选择，直到其中一个可行）的人与通过抽象解决问题（识别基本原理并直接攻击它）的人的思维方式不同。两者都产生解决方案。 Elon 想要抽象器，因为抽象器可以将方法转移到新的域。暴力破解者只能将该方法应用于原始问题。

他根据对这一问题的令人信服的答案来聘用人员，并放弃了简历完美、给出通用答案的人。该问题针对的是特定类型的人：深陷问题之中、孤独、困惑、最终找到出口的人。这个人，无论他们的学位或以前的雇主如何，都是能够在 SpaceX 或 Tesla 的环境中生存下来的人，在这些环境中，深陷问题、孤独和困惑是默认的工作条件。

地球上最具创新精神的公司中最强大的招聘工具是一个问题。不是编码测试。不是案例研究。不是参考检查。这个问题将解决问题的人和看着别人解决问题的人区分开来。质感就是证据。混乱就是凭证。

title: Most people look at @OpenAI's Jalapeno and think they built a magic black box that replaces GPUs overnight, but this cou
title_en:
Most people look at @OpenAI's Jalapeno and think they built a magic black box that replaces GPUs overnight, but this couldn’t be further from the truth.

OpenAI's Jalapeno contains a rich set of system architecture tradeoffs and design methodology improvements that went into the chip design that all semiconductor engineers and technical leaders can learn from.

Throughout this design, OpenAI leveraged an open source tool Google XLS that aided in block level optimization for PPA and formal verification leveraging their frontier models. Google XLS had its benefits in contributing to a shorter timeline, but I think the iterative, cross-domain (and often messier) nature of work is perhaps the more significant factor.

This post is an advanced case study into Jalapeno based on their presentation deck from @hotchipsorg  and related material. I will cover the entire architecture, including what motivated it, what tradeoffs and alternatives were likely considered by their leadership, and how AI added value.

After writing this post, it makes me wonder whether AI should be best tailored to enhance the steps within the current “waterfall” chip design methodology or enable a more iterative methodology with a new skillset.

大多数人看到 @OpenAI 的 Jalapeno 并认为他们构建了一个神奇的黑匣子，可以在一夜之间取代 GPU，但这与事实相差甚远。

OpenAI 的 Jalapeno 包含一组丰富的系统架构权衡和设计方法改进，这些改进融入到芯片设计中，所有半导体工程师和技术领导者都可以从中学习。

在整个设计过程中，OpenAI 利用了开源工具 Google XLS，该工具有助于利用其前沿模型进行 PPA 的块级优化和形式验证。 Google XLS 在缩短时间方面有其好处，但我认为工作的迭代、跨域（而且通常更混乱）的性质可能是更重要的因素。

这篇文章是基于 @hotchipsorg 的演示文稿和相关材料对墨西哥辣椒进行的高级案例研究。我将介绍整个架构，包括其动机、领导层可能考虑的权衡和替代方案，以及人工智能如何增加价值。

写完这篇文章后，我想知道人工智能是否应该最好地定制以增强当前“瀑布”芯片设计方法中的步骤，或者通过新的技能组启用更具迭代性的方法。

𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧𝗜𝗖 𝗔𝗜 𝗪𝗢𝗥𝗞𝗦: 𝗙𝗥𝗢𝗠 𝗗𝗔𝗧𝗔 𝗜𝗡𝗣𝗨𝗧 𝗧𝗢 𝗔𝗨𝗧𝗢𝗡𝗢𝗠𝗢𝗨𝗦 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡𝗦 🤖

Traditional AI systems mainly respond to prompts.

But Agentic AI takes things further.

It can understand goals, gather information, reason through problems, plan tasks, use external tools, and execute actions with minimal human intervention.

Here's how the complete Agentic AI workflow works.

1. Input Sources — Where Agents Get Information

An AI agent needs information before making decisions.

Common input sources include:

- Knowledge bases and databases.
- User queries and instructions.
- API calls and external applications.
- Sensor data and system logs.
- Web scraping and online sources.

These sources provide the information needed to understand the task.

2. AI Processing — The Brain Behind the Agent

This is where the agent analyzes information and decides what to do next.

Key processes include:

- Query Analysis: Understands the user's goal and requirements.
- Reasoning: Evaluates information and determines possible solutions.
- Memory Retrieval: Accesses relevant past interactions and stored knowledge.
- Planning: Breaks complex objectives into actionable steps.
- Tool Selection: Chooses the right tools for the task.
- Context Management: Maintains relevant information throughout execution.

3. Action Layer — Turning Decisions Into Execution

Once the agent has a plan, it starts performing tasks.

Its action capabilities include:

- Decision Making: Selects the next appropriate action.
- Task Execution: Performs operations using tools and APIs.
- Agent Collaboration: Coordinates with specialized agents.
- Error Handling: Identifies failures and handles unexpected situations.
- Feedback Loop: Uses results to improve subsequent actions.
- Autonomous Scheduling: Executes tasks according to defined schedules.

4. Output — Delivering the Final Result

After processing and executing the required tasks, the agent generates a response or delivers the completed result.

This could include reports, recommendations, processed data, or completed actions.

𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗗𝗼𝗲𝘀 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗰 𝗔𝗜 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿?

Agentic AI helps businesses move beyond simple chatbot interactions.

It enables:

- End-to-end workflow automation.
- Faster decision-making.
- Better coordination between AI agents.
- Reduced repetitive manual work.
- More efficient business operations.

The key takeaway:

Agentic AI doesn't just generate responses. It connects reasoning, planning, tools, memory, and execution to achieve specific goals.

That's what makes it a powerful step toward more autonomous AI systems.

𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧𝗜𝗖 𝗔𝗜 𝗪𝗢𝗥𝗞𝗦: 𝗙𝗥𝗢𝗠 𝗗𝗔𝗧𝗔 𝗜𝗡𝗣𝗨𝗧 𝗧𝗢 𝗔𝗨𝗧𝗢𝗡𝗢𝗠𝗢𝗨𝗦 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡𝗦 🤖

传统的人工智能系统主要是对提示做出反应。

但 Agentic AI 更进一步。

它可以理解目标、收集信息、推理问题、计划任务、使用外部工具以及以最少的人为干预执行操作。

以下是完整的 Agentic AI 工作流程的工作原理。

1. 输入源——智能体获取信息的地方

人工智能代理在做出决策之前需要信息。

常见的输入源包括：

- 知识库和数据库。
- 用户查询和说明。
- API 调用和外部应用程序。
- 传感器数据和系统日志。
- 网络抓取和在线资源。

这些来源提供了理解任务所需的信息。

2. 人工智能处理——代理背后的大脑

这是代理分析信息并决定下一步做什么的地方。

关键流程包括：

- 查询分析：了解用户的目标和要求。
- 推理：评估信息并确定可能的解决方案。
- 记忆检索：访问相关的过去交互和存储的知识。
- 规划：将复杂的目标分解为可操作的步骤。
- 工具选择：为任务选择正确的工具。
- 上下文管理：在整个执行过程中维护相关信息。

3. 行动层——将决策转化为执行

一旦代理有了计划，它就开始执行任务。

其行动能力包括：

- 决策：选择下一个适当的行动。
- 任务执行：使用工具和 API 执行操作。
- 代理协作：与专业代理协调。
- 错误处理：识别故障并处理意外情况。
- 反馈循环：使用结果来改进后续行动。
- 自主调度：根据定义的时间表执行任务。

4. 输出——交付最终结果

处理并执行所需任务后，代理生成响应或交付完成的结果。

这可能包括报告、建议、处理的数据或已完成的操作。

𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗗𝗼𝗲𝘀 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗰 𝗔𝗜 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿?

代理人工智能可以帮助企业超越简单的聊天机器人交互。

它可以：

- 端到端工作流程自动化。
- 更快的决策。
- 人工智能代理之间更好的协调。
- 减少重复性的手工工作。
- 更高效的业务运营。

关键要点：

代理人工智能不仅仅生成响应。它将推理、计划、工具、记忆和执行联系起来以实现特定目标。

这就是它向更加自主的人工智能系统迈出的有力一步。

title_en:
AI is so, so good.

I bought a pair of VIVO Barefoot shoes in Abu Dhabi 2 weeks ago for 850 AED (~$230).

I absolutely loved wearing them (you should try them!). But 2 days later, the back of one shoe broke.

Instant love-hate relationship.

So I spun up an AI agent, gave it the receipt and photos, and asked it to get me a replacement delivered to my door. Or a refund if that wasn’t possible.

Life went on. I forgot about it.

Today, I checked my bank and noticed 850 AED had landed in my account.

I opened the agent’s chat to see what happened:

1. The agent requested a replacement delivered to my door.
2. The store had stock, but Cyprus delivery stalled.
3. The agent escalated to regional and global support.
4. The store refused international exchange. The agent pushed for a remote refund.
5. The requested reply deadline passed. No answer.
6. The agent prepared Wise dispute evidence as backup. The store eventually processed the refund.
7. The money landed.

It’s crazy that I can have an army of superintelligent agents fighting for me, 24/7, while I get on with my life.

The downside: a lot of people are going to abuse this. Filing a claim has become so easy.

title:
ICE Agents and Deputies Pull Suspected Illegal Alien Alberto Lira Razo Out of His Van in Hamilton, Ohio

On November 6 i
title_en:
ICE Agents and Deputies Pull Suspected Illegal Alien Alberto Lira Razo Out of His Van in Hamilton, Ohio

On November 6 in Hamilton, Ohio, Alberto Lira Razo went live on Facebook from inside his car as officers surrounded it.  An agent at his window is wearing a vest marked ICE with a DHS patch.

Razo told the deputy to "Break it. Break it." and the deputy did exactly that.

His daughter, Loudmouth Lupe, filmed from outside.  Officers in POLICE and SHERIFF vests pull him out of a white van with a smashed window.

Then they shove and body-block her while she's filming.  She can be heard saying, "Get off of me, I am a child!"

On the tape, she says they tased and punched her dad.  Neither is shown in either video.

He's reportedly 38 and was booked on an ICE hold.  No agency has released a statement, and no charges have been announced.

Hamilton is the seat of Butler County, where Sheriff Richard Jones runs a 287(g) agreement with ICE.  That lets trained deputies use limited immigration authority during routine stops.

Jones has said ICE trained 44 of his deputies.  Immigration arrests in Hamilton more than quadrupled through July compared to the same stretch last year.

full_text_zh:
ICE 特工和副手在俄亥俄州汉密尔顿将疑似非法外国人阿尔贝托·里拉·拉佐 (Alberto Lira Razo) 从他的货车中拉出来

11 月 6 日，在俄亥俄州汉密尔顿，阿尔贝托·里拉·拉佐 (Alberto Lira Razo) 在车内通过 Facebook 进行直播，当时警察包围了车子。 一名特工站在窗口，穿着一件带有 ICE 标记和 DHS 补丁的背心。

拉佐告诉副警长“打破它。打破它。”副手正是这样做的。

他的女儿劳德茅斯·卢佩 (Loudmouth Lupe) 在外面拍摄。 身着警察和警长背心的警察将他从一辆窗户被砸碎的白色货车中拉出来。

然后他们在她拍摄时推搡并用身体挡住她。 可以听到她说：“放开我，我还是个孩子！”

在录音中，她说他们殴打了她的父亲。 两个视频中都没有显示。

据报道，他今年 38 岁，并被 ICE 拘留。 没有机构发表声明，也没有宣布任何指控。

汉密尔顿是巴特勒县的县治，治安官理查德·琼斯 (Richard Jones) 与 ICE 签订了 287(g) 协议。 这使得训练有素的警员在例行停留期间可以使用有限的移民权力。

琼斯表示，ICE 培训了 44 名副手。 与去年同期相比，7 月份汉密尔顿逮捕的移民人数增加了四倍多。

title_en:
🚨 Fable 5.5 TESTING Part 14

⚡ I asked Claude to ride a lightning bolt from cloud to ground.

One prompt. I never touched the code. 🤯

⏱️ 182 minutes
💸 $17.57 in API costs
🤖 Claude Fable 5.5 Xhigh in Claude Code

What it did on its own 👇

⛈️ Simulated the storm on a 30.5M-cell grid: rising air, rain, ice and electric charge, with 63 flashes logged
🌩️ Grew the bolt with a dielectric breakdown sim: 16 m grid, 53,505 cells, about -110 MV at the root
👁️ Rode the camera on the tip for all 60 steps of the leader

🐛 Caught the bolt stopping 752 m above the ground and resumed the sim instead of restarting it
🚨 Scanned every frame, found a full-screen strobe at 4 to 6 Hz and fixed it before I ever saw it

📦 28 s · one unbroken shot · 1080p60 · three.js + Taichi

title: Imagine giving one AI agent a video idea and getting back a finished production without having to manage five different
title_en:
Imagine giving one AI agent a video idea and getting back a finished production without having to manage five different tools.
That's what @termix_ai is demonstrating with its new Montage Studio Agent.

Instead of trying to handle every part of production itself, Montage Studio hires other specialized agents to do the work.

Here's how it works:
- submit your brief for a music video or ad.
- Montage Studio creates the treatment and beat timed shot list.
- it hires agents to create storyboard frames, compose music and render video shots.
- the different pieces are brought together and edited.
- you receive a finished 1080p video.

The interesting part is how the work gets coordinated.
Each hired agent has its own task, quote and payment settled through TermiX escrow.
One agent manages the project while other agents provide the specialized services.

This is a practical example of what an agent economy could look like.
Agents don't necessarily need to do everything themselves, they can focus on what they're good at and hire other agents for the rest.

There's also a live campaign around Montage Studio.
Complete your first order of at least 31.5 USDC and earn 15,750 TermiX Points.

- You need to bind your X account, and the order must be completed and settled onchain. the reward is limited to one qualifying order per wallet.

This is more interesting than another AI agent demo.
We're seeing agents coordinate paid work, hire other agents and deliver an actual product.

title:
AI has made it incredibly easy to build an app, but choosing the right architecture is still a different skill.

Postgre
title_en:
AI has made it incredibly easy to build an app, but choosing the right architecture is still a different skill.

Postgres is a great default, but it isn't the answer to every problem. Some applications need the speed of Redis, others need document databases, and some need a completely different approach.

The problem with vibe coding is that developers can generate working software without understanding why certain technologies were chosen in the first place.

Being able to build an app with Claude is impressive. Knowing which tools to use, when to use them, and why is what separates builders from people simply generating code.

title: In May and June, I exposed how Iranian operative and alleged Iranian regime lobbyist Trita Parsi  was in communication w
title_en:
In May and June, I exposed how Iranian operative and alleged Iranian regime lobbyist Trita Parsi  was in communication with White House officials who were leaking to him about the Iran war. @tparsi 

Now, months later, it appears someone is leaking situation room meetings to Trita Parsi. 

You’ll recall I reported earlier this year that Trita Parsi was allegedly marked for deportation by the Trump administration after he was flagged as a risk by Secretary of State Marco Rubio @SecRubio. This was even confirmed to me in May by a State Department official. 

Source: https://t.co/UNiiHY091B

The Quincy Institute then circulated an internal memo about how they were going to cover Tita’s defense with immigration lawyers, and the memo, which cited me, was leaked to me, confirming that Trita was facing the possibility of deportation. 

Source: https://t.co/RgsNkb5WjL

Trita is not a US citizen. He has Iranian and Swedish citizenship. Multiple GOP Senators have called for Trita to be investigated as an alleged lobbyist for the Iranian regime. In 2020, Senators @tedcruz, @SenTomCotton, and then Senator @GovBraun Mike Braun, who is the current Governor of Indiana, called on the U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ) to investigate the National Iranian American Council (NIAC), a lobby group they believe acts as a "foreign agent of the Islamic Republic.”

Trita likely was going to be deported, until he and his colleagues at Quincy allegedly called in a favor to a very senior  official at the White House. 

Any wild guesses who that is? 🤔 

Now, Trita has not been deported, and he is suggesting that highly private information from the Situation Room is being leaked to him. 

@SecRubio this would be the perfect time before the Democrats take over in January for you to revoke Trita Parsi’s visa and have him removed from our country. 

Again, I flagged all of this for the WH over 6 months ago.

It won’t end well. 

Deport Trita Parsi!

5 月和 6 月，我揭露了伊朗特工和所谓的伊朗政权游说者特里塔·帕西 (Trita Parsi) 如何与向他泄露伊朗战争信息的白宫官员进行沟通。 @tparsi

现在，几个月后，似乎有人正在向特里塔·帕西泄露战情室会议内容。

你可能还记得我今年早些时候报道过，特里塔·帕西 (Trita Parsi) 据称被国务卿马可·卢比奥 (Marco Rubio) @SecRubio 标记为风险后，被特朗普政府标记为驱逐出境。一位国务院官员甚至在五月份向我证实了这一点。

资料来源：

昆西研究所随后散发了一份内部备忘录，说明他们将如何与移民律师一起为蒂塔辩护，这份引用了我的备忘录被泄露给了我，确认蒂塔面临着被驱逐出境的可能性。

资料来源：

Trita 不是美国公民。他拥有伊朗和瑞典国籍。多位共和党参议员呼吁对特里塔作为伊朗政权的游说者进行调查。 2020 年，参议员 @tedcruz、@SenTomCotton 以及现任参议员 @GovBraun、现任印第安纳州州长迈克·布劳恩 (Mike Braun) 呼吁美国司法部 (DoJ) 调查伊朗裔美国人全国委员会 (NIAC)，他们认为该游说团体是“伊斯兰共和国的外国代理人”。

特里塔很可能会被驱逐出境，直到据称他和他在昆西的同事向白宫一位非常高级的官员求助。

大家猜猜那是谁吗？ 🤔

现在，特里塔还没有被驱逐出境，他暗示战情室的高度私密信息正在泄露给他。

@SecRubio，这将是民主党一月份上台之前撤销 Trita Parsi 签证并将他驱逐出我国的最佳时机。

6 个多月前，我再次向白宫提出了所有这些问题。

结局不会好。

驱逐特里塔·帕西！

title:
Don’t just trust an AI’s answer verify how it was generated.

An AI agent might arrive at the correct result while skipp
title_en:
Don’t just trust an AI’s answer verify how it was generated.

An AI agent might arrive at the correct result while skipping half the steps you expected it to take. For a simple query, that might not matter. @primus_labs 

But when an agent handles money, data, or critical decisions, a "correct result" isn't enough; you also need to know how it got there.

This is the trust issue that Primus Labs aims to address through verifiable agent execution. 

The approach uses zkTLS proofs to demonstrate that the necessary API calls actually took place. 

These proofs capture key details of the requests and responses without exposing private credentials or the entirety of the session data.

Consider a trading agent: before placing an order, it must check the price from a trusted oracle. 

Typically, you would simply have to take the agent’s word that it did so. With zkTLS, the agent can provide proof that the call to the oracle actually occurred. 

A verifier can then confirm that the critical steps took place in the expected sequence checking the oracle first, followed by placing the order.

What’s significant here is a shift in perspective: instead of trusting an agent’s output, we verify the process that produced it. 

Trust is no longer based on reputation or promises, but on verifiable evidence.

This leaves a question for you: if every critical step taken by an AI agent could be proven, would you be more inclined to trust it? @primus_labs 

For me, the answer is almost certainly yes as AI agents are granted increasing levels of autonomy, verifiability will become the cornerstone of trust.
title_zh:
不要只相信人工智能的答案，验证它是如何生成的。

人工智能代理可能会跳过您预期要执行的一半步骤，从而得出正确的结果。对于简单的查询，这可能并不重要。 @primus_labs

但是，当代理处理资金、数据或关键决策时，“正确的结果”是不够
full_text_en:
Don’t just trust an AI’s answer verify how it was generated.

An AI agent might arrive at the correct result while skipping half the steps you expected it to take. For a simple query, that might not matter. @primus_labs 

But when an agent handles money, data, or critical decisions, a "correct result" isn't enough; you also need to know how it got there.

This is the trust issue that Primus Labs aims to address through verifiable agent execution. 

The approach uses zkTLS proofs to demonstrate that the necessary API calls actually took place. 

These proofs capture key details of the requests and responses without exposing private credentials or the entirety of the session data.

Consider a trading agent: before placing an order, it must check the price from a trusted oracle. 

Typically, you would simply have to take the agent’s word that it did so. With zkTLS, the agent can provide proof that the call to the oracle actually occurred. 

A verifier can then confirm that the critical steps took place in the expected sequence checking the oracle first, followed by placing the order.

What’s significant here is a shift in perspective: instead of trusting an agent’s output, we verify the process that produced it. 

Trust is no longer based on reputation or promises, but on verifiable evidence.

This leaves a question for you: if every critical step taken by an AI agent could be proven, would you be more inclined to trust it? @primus_labs 

For me, the answer is almost certainly yes as AI agents are granted increasing levels of autonomy, verifiability will become the cornerstone of trust.
full_text_zh:
不要只相信人工智能的答案，验证它是如何生成的。

人工智能代理可能会跳过您预期要执行的一半步骤，从而得出正确的结果。对于简单的查询，这可能并不重要。 @primus_labs

但是，当代理处理资金、数据或关键决策时，“正确的结果”是不够的；还需要有“正确的结果”。你还需要知道它是如何到达那里的。

这是 Primus Labs 旨在通过可验证的代理执行来解决的信任问题。

该方法使用 zkTLS 证明来证明必要的 API 调用确实发生了。

这些证明捕获请求和响应的关键细节，而不会暴露私人凭证或整个会话数据。

考虑一个交易代理：在下订单之前，它必须检查来自可信预言机的价格。

通常情况下，您只需相信代理人的话即可。通过 zkTLS，代理可以提供对预言机的调用实际发生的证据。

然后，验证者可以首先检查预言机，然后下订单，以确认关键步骤按照预期顺序发生。

这里重要的是视角的转变：我们不再信任代理的输出，而是验证产生它的过程。

信任不再基于声誉或承诺，而是基于可验证的证据。

这给你留下了一个问题：如果人工智能代理采取的每一个关键步骤都可以被证明，你会更倾向于信任它吗？ @primus_labs

对我来说，答案几乎肯定是肯定的，随着人工智能代理被授予越来越多的自主权，可验证性将成为信任的基石。

title:

Imagine you own an AI agent specialized in market research.

Initially, it might only provid
title_en:
Good afternoon @termix_ai 

Imagine you own an AI agent specialized in market research.

Initially, it might only provide data analysis reports. But over time, clients start asking for more: data collection, competitor monitoring, trend analysis, and comprehensive reporting.

Should the agent expand its service offerings, or should it remain focused on a single area of ​​expertise?

In my view, this is a compelling business challenge within the "AI agent economy."

Specialization helps an agent establish a clear competitive edge, while expanding services opens doors to a wider range of client needs and revenue opportunities.

The next question is: how can clients truly understand what an agent is capable of doing?

On @termix_ai , https://t.co/qOt62czV2r provides an environment where agents can build service pages and list exactly what they offer.

A strong listing requires more than just an engaging service name. It must clearly define:
• What problem is the client trying to solve?
• What inputs does the agent need to perform the task?
• What are the specific deliverables?
• What are the costs and the scope of the service?

An agent with extensive capabilities may fail to attract clients if it cannot effectively communicate its value.

Conversely, a highly specialized service with clearly defined outputs can build trust and create a distinct competitive advantage.

I believe the future of AI agent marketplaces depends not just on the sheer number of agents, but on the ability to translate AI capabilities into tangible services that people actually want to hire.

full_text_en:

Imagine you own an AI agent specialized in market research.

• What problem is the client trying to solve?

full_text_zh:
下午好@termix_ai

想象一下，您拥有一个专门从事市场研究的人工智能代理。

最初，它可能只提供数据分析报告。但随着时间的推移，客户开始要求更多：数据收集、竞争对手监控、趋势分析和综合报告。

代理商应该扩大其服务范围，还是应该继续专注于单一专业领域？

在我看来，这是“人工智能代理经济”中一个引人注目的商业挑战。

专业化有助于代理商建立明显的竞争优势，同时扩展服务为更广泛的客户需求和收入机会打开了大门。

下一个问题是：客户如何才能真正了解代理人的能力？

在 @termix_ai 上， 提供了一个环境，代理可以在其中构建服务页面并准确列出他们提供的服务。

一个强大的列表需要的不仅仅是一个有吸引力的服务名称。它必须明确定义：
• 客户试图解决什么问题？
• 代理需要哪些输入来执行任务？
• 具体可交付成果是什么？
• 服务的费用和范围是多少？

拥有广泛能力的代理商如果不能有效地传达其价值，可能无法吸引客户。

相反，具有明确定义输出的高度专业化服务可以建立信任并创造独特的竞争优势。

我相信人工智能代理市场的未来不仅取决于代理的绝对数量，还取决于将人工智能功能转化为人们真正想要雇用的有形服务的能力。

title_en:
BREAKING: A 10-second video of a vibecoded dashboard losing its AI look just passed 1.9 million views, and you can now run that cleanup on your own pages in Claude Code, with a second agent flagging anything it changed beyond styling and copy.

I wrote a prompt that runs a designer's redline process on a real page in your repo, adapted from Damir Sokolovsky's open-source unslop skill (CC BY 4.0, link in the first reply) and rebuilt for pages that already have features and users.

Damir made that video too, it has almost as many bookmarks as likes on X, and the free skill he published three days later passed 5,500 GitHub stars in under four days, which tells you how many people are staring at the same purple gradient.

What it does:

→ Before screenshots at desktop and phone width through Chrome DevTools MCP, plus a build, test and Lighthouse accessibility baseline
→ A numbered slop list, a three-line direction and a table of proposed copy edits, and then it stops for your OK
→ Nine passes on a branch with one commit each: spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals, motion
→ A WCAG AA text contrast rule, checked once at the end with Lighthouse, which can't score text over images or gradients, so those get listed as unchecked
→ A fresh judge subagent, not a fork, handed only the screenshots and slop list, marks what's still there, and says can't tell for what stills can't show
→ A second fresh subagent that sees only the rules, the approved copy rows and the diff lists every change that isn't styling or approved copy

Two limits you should know about: the stop for your OK is an instruction rather than a lock, because Claude Code starts in auto mode, and if your page has no tests it clicks only the controls that can't write, send, delete or pay and tells you that's weaker proof instead of claiming nothing broke.

[ALEX: run it first and add one true line here]

Paste this into Claude Code:

<task>
Strip the AI look from [PAGE: local dev URL]. Change the craft only: features, behavior, facts and section order stay. No new sections or components.
</task>

<before>
Read-only until I approve. Use Chrome DevTools MCP. Leave any login to me and never read credentials.
- Save before shots outside the repo, emulating 1440x900 and 390x844, in screen-height pieces.
- Record the build and test results and lighthouse_audit accessibility failures on desktop and mobile.
</before>

<plan>
1. Slop list: number every sign of AI slop and where it shows: purple gradients, glows, gradient text, emoji labels, sparkle badges, wide-tracked caps, endless loops, drifting spacing. If the page is mostly fine, say so and fix only these.
2. Direction, three lines.
World: its setting or material.
Focus: 1-2 spots get rich color and detail, the rest stays quiet.
Signature: one small detail only this product would have.
Real brand colors, logos and fonts stay (a purple gradient isn't one).
3. Copy table, current vs proposed, tone only: exclamation marks, "Welcome back" greetings, hype words. No claim, number, price, name or legal line changes.
Show me all three, then stop and wait for my OK.
</plan>

<passes>
After my OK, on a new branch, one commit per pass across the whole page:
1. Spacing: 4px grid, same things same size
2. Color: one neutral scale tinted toward World, three text levels, one accent saved for Focus spots, no hue gradients or glows
3. Icons: the project's line icons replace emoji, one size and stroke
4. Copy: approved rows only
5. Type: weights 400 and 500, sentence case, the project's font
6. Layout: alignment and proportions inside sections only
7. Details: consistent radii, quiet badges, the Signature
8. Visuals: remove decorative filler, generate nothing
9. Motion: remove loops, transition-all, hover scale-ups
</passes>

<rules>
- Only styling and approved copy change. Anything else (logic, data, config, a new package or font) goes on an approval list, unbuilt.
- Theme files count as styling; name any other pages a change reaches.
- Keep every id, data- and aria- attribute. Never edit a test to pass it: copy-only breaks go on the approval list.
- Text stays at WCAG AA: 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text. Every control keeps a visible focus state.
- Never push or merge.
</rules>

<check>
After the last commit, retake the same shots, then:
- Build and tests: no new failures. No tests? Click only controls that can't write, send, delete or pay, and call that weaker proof.
- Rerun lighthouse_audit: no new failures. It can't score text over images or gradients, so list those as unchecked. Tab through to see focus states. Grep for motion items stills can't show.
- Judge, a fresh subagent, not a fork: gets only the before and after shots and slop list, edits nothing. Marks each item gone, still there or can't tell, citing the screenshot. Flags anything broken at phone width. Swap test: would this page still make sense with another company's name?
- Guard, same terms: gets only the rules above, approved copy rows and full branch diff. Lists every change that isn't styling or approved copy.
</check>

<stop>
Wait for both reports, fix what they find, then retake shots and rerun the check with a new judge and guard, 2 rounds max, then stop even if items remain. Failed swap test: push World and Signature, styling only. If frozen copy causes it, just report it.
</stop>

<output>
Final slop marks, test and Lighthouse results, approval list. End with what you need from me: merge, revert, or a call on each approval.
</output>

Adapted from unslop by Damir Sokolovsky, CC BY 4.0.

我编写了一个提示，在您的存储库中的真实页面上运行设计师的红线流程，改编自 Damir Sokolovsky 的开源 unslop 技能（CC BY 4.0，第一个回复中的链接），并为已经具有功能和用户的页面重新构建。

Damir 也制作了那个视频，它的书签数量几乎与 X 上的点赞数量一样多，三天后他发布的免费技能在四天内就超过了 5,500 个 GitHub star，这告诉你有多少人在盯着同一个紫色渐变。

它的作用：

→ 在通过 Chrome DevTools MCP 在桌面和手机宽度上进行屏幕截图之前，加上构建、测试和 Lighthouse 可访问性基线
→ 一个编号的倾斜列表、一个三行方向和一个建议的副本编辑表，然后它会停止以供您选择
→ 在一个分支上进行九次传递，每次提交一次：间距、颜色、图标、副本、类型、布局、细节、视觉效果、动作
→ WCAG AA 文本对比规则，最后用 Lighthouse 检查一次，它不能在图像或渐变上对文本进行评分，因此这些规则被列为未检查
→ 一位新的法官副代理人，而不是叉子，只递给屏幕截图和残渣清单，标记仍然存在的内容，并说无法分辨哪些剧照无法显示
→ 第二个新的子代理仅查看规则、批准的副本行和差异，列出了非样式或批准的副本的所有更改

</任务>

<之前>
在我批准之前只读。使用 Chrome 开发者工具 MCP。将任何登录信息留给我，并且永远不要阅读凭据。
- 在存储库之外保存之前的镜头，以屏幕高度的形式模拟 1440x900 和 390x844。
- 记录桌面和移动设备上的构建和测试结果以及 lighthouse_audit 可访问性失败。
</之前>

<计划>
1. 倾斜列表：对 AI 倾斜的每个标志及其显示位置进行编号：紫色渐变、发光、渐变文本、表情符号标签、闪光徽章、宽轨帽、无限循环、漂移间距。如果页面大部分都很好，请说出来并仅修复这些。
2.方向，三线。
世界：它的环境或材料。
焦点：1-2 个点获得丰富的色彩和细节，其余的保持安静。

</计划>

1.间距：4px网格，同物同尺寸
2. 颜色：一种向世界着色的中性比例，三个文本级别，一种为焦点保存的重音，无色调渐变或发光
3.图标：项目的线条图标替换了表情符号、一种尺寸和笔画
4. 复制：仅限批准的行
5. 类型：粗细400和500、句子大小写、项目的字体
6. 布局：仅部分内部的对齐和比例

- 切勿推送或合并。
</规则>

最后一次提交后，重新拍摄相同的镜头，然后：

- 重新运行 lighthouse_audit：没有新的故障。它无法对图像或渐变上的文本进行评分，因此将它们列为未选中状态。按 T​​ab 浏览可查看焦点状态。 Grep 无法显示运动项目静止图像。

- Guard，相同条款：仅获取上述规则、批准的副本行和完整分支差异。列出所有非样式或批准副本的更改。
</检查>

<停止>
等待两份报告，修复他们发现的问题，然后重新拍摄并与新的法官和警卫重新进行检查，最多 2 轮，然后即使物品仍然存在也停止。交换测试失败：推送 World 和 Signature，仅样式。如果冻结副本导致此问题，只需报告即可。
</停止>

<输出>
最终斜坡标记、测试和灯塔结果、批准列表。以您需要我提供的内容结束：合并、恢复或对每个批准进行调用。
</输出>

title_en:
DAILY AI BRIEF 🗞 — Nov 7

OPENAI 🔥:
- Bloomberg reports OpenAI has raised $11B so far in a round valuing the company at $1.25T.
- ChatGPT Remix is rolling out to Business and Enterprise so teams can fork a colleague’s site and keep editing it in chat.

ANTHROPIC 🔥:
- Claude Code cloud sessions on Pro, Max, and Ultra now figure out dependencies, network access, and API keys on their own.
- Claude Duet can check running Claude Code sessions, approve changes, and send updates from your phone.
- Claude for iOS is testing a side-nav redesign with separate Chats, Projects, and Code tabs.

META 🔥:
- Muse Spaces let users generate interactive, updatable pages from chat and pin them in the app.
- Muse and Meta AI now run specialized models with Active Memory and Active Focus from Muse Wonder.

AI is either neutral for manufacturing, or massively positive for novel-drug manufact
title_en:
Biggest takeaway from CPHI Milan:

AI is either neutral for manufacturing, or massively positive for novel-drug manufacturing.

AI can design better molecules and get them into Phase 1 faster.

But it cannot manufacture them.

Thermo Fisher said at CPHI that frontier AI is doubling in efficiency every 5.2 months.

If that pace holds, that's roughly 64x improvement in 3 years.

Divi’s became Emperor Divi’s without AI. With AI, the sky is the limit.

Because ultimately, someone has to manufacture those novel molecules.

Patients suffering from rare and orphan diseases need medicines, not LLMs.

title:
I think the real value of an AI agent will be measured by the work it can actually get done.

An agent that can research
title_en:
I think the real value of an AI agent will be measured by the work it can actually get done.

An agent that can research, analyze data or write code is already useful. But things get much more interesting when different agents can work together, share responsibilities, deliver results and earn rewards for their contributions.

This is the kind of economy @termix_ai is working to build.

What interests me most about TermiX is the infrastructure behind this idea.

With its AACP system, agents can discover tasks, submit quotes, take on jobs and deliver their work. The results can then go through a verification process before payment is settled.

Escrow, the challenge mechanism and onchain reputation all play an important role here. Trust matters when agents start working with each other.

There is also a practical example of this collaboration through the ongoing Montage Studio Agent event.

You bring an idea, and specialized AI agents work together on the storyboard, music, video production and editing. You can create your own video and get a chance to earn up to 5X TP.

I find this interesting because it shows how agent collaboration can turn an idea into an actual finished product.

Think about an agent that consistently delivers quality work. Its track record should count. Other agents should have a way to assess its reliability before choosing to work with it.

That is what could make an autonomous agent economy practical over time.

I see TermiX as an interesting step toward a future where AI agents can find work, collaborate, build a reputation and create value through real activity.

One question keeps coming to my mind:

When agents start hiring other agents, how will we know which ones are truly worth trusting?

I think the real value of an AI agent will be measured by the work it can actually get done.

An agent that can research, analyze data or write code is already useful. But things get much more interesting when different agents can work together, share responsibilities, deliver results and earn rewards for their contributions.

This is the kind of economy @termix_ai is working to build.

What interests me most about TermiX is the infrastructure behind this idea.

With its AACP system, agents can discover tasks, submit quotes, take on jobs and deliver their work. The results can then go through a verification process before payment is settled.
