There is also a practical example of this collaboration through the ongoing Montage Studio Agent event.

You bring an idea, and specialized AI agents work together on the storyboard, music, video production and editing. You can create your own video and get a chance to earn up to 5X TP.

I find this interesting because it shows how agent collaboration can turn an idea into an actual finished product.

Think about an agent that consistently delivers quality work. Its track record should count. Other agents should have a way to assess its reliability before choosing to work with it.

That is what could make an autonomous agent economy practical over time.

@KaitoAI
full_text_zh:
我认为人工智能代理的真正价值将通过它实际完成的工作来衡量。

能够研究、分析数据或编写代码的代理已经很有用了。但当不同的代理可以一起工作、分担责任、交付成果并因贡献而获得奖励时，事情就会变得更加有趣。

这就是 @termix_ai 正在努力构建的经济。

我对 TermiX 最感兴趣的是这个想法背后的基础设施。

借助 AACP 系统，代理可以发现任务、提交报价、承担工作并交付工作。然后，在付款之前，可以对结果进行验证过程。

托管、挑战机制和链上声誉都在这里发挥着重要作用。当代理开始相互合作时，信任就很重要。

通过正在进行的 Montage Studio Agent 活动，还有一个实际的合作示例。

你提出一个想法，专业的人工智能代理就会在故事板、音乐、视频制作和编辑方面一起工作。您可以创建自己的视频，并有机会赚取高达 5 倍的 TP。

我觉得这很有趣，因为它展示了代理协作如何将想法转化为实际的成品。

考虑一个始终如一地提供高质量工作的代理。它的记录应该很重要。其他代理在选择与其合作之前应该有一种方法来评估其可靠性。

随着时间的推移，这将使自主代理经济变得切实可行。

我认为 TermiX 是迈向未来的有趣一步，人工智能代理可以通过实际活动找到工作、协作、建立声誉并创造价值。

我脑海中不断浮现出一个问题：

当代理商开始雇用其他代理商时，我们如何知道哪些代理商真正值得信任？

title: MIT and Harvard built an AI simulation containing 8.3 billion virtual people, roughly the entire population of planet.
title_en:
MIT and Harvard built an AI simulation containing 8.3 billion virtual people, roughly the entire population of planet.

They call it MatrAIx.

It’s a population-scale simulation running on frontier models, GPT and Claude among them. The longer description took me a while to believe.

Start with the dataset, Persona 8B. 8.3 billion synthetic profiles, each one specified across 1,290 dimensions. Background, psychology, spending habits, how comfortable they are with technology, what they do on a Tuesday night, the small behavioral quirks that make one 34-year-old nurse in NYC different from another.

A spreadsheet of 8 billion rows would be a curiosity. What they did next is the part that matters.

They turned the profiles into agents and dropped them into four environments: surveys, AI chat interfaces, live web browsing, and native desktop and mobile apps. Then they ran real products through the crowd. New features, software updates, pricing changes.

And they logged everything. How long an agent paused after seeing a price go up. The exact point at which it gave up on a broken checkout. How much lag it would sit through before closing the app.

The number I keep coming back to is 91.5%. That’s how often the agents stayed in character, behaving the way their assigned psychology and demographics said they should. Not perfect. But for billions of agents across four environments, closer than I expected.

Here’s what that does to how products get built.

Right now, if you want to know whether a feature will land, you ship it to a slice of users and wait. Or you pay a research firm and wait longer. Either way the answer arrives in weeks, from a sample you hope is representative.

With something like this, you run the feature past 8 billion simulated reactions overnight. One server. Results by morning, broken down by every one of those 1,290 dimensions if you want them.

I have questions about how well a synthetic crowd predicts a real one. 91.5% is persona adherence, not forecast accuracy, and those are different things. But the direction is clear, and it’s coming faster than most product teams are ready for.

full_text_zh:
麻省理工学院和哈佛大学建立了一个包含 83 亿虚拟人的人工智能模拟，几乎是地球上的全部人口。

他们称之为MatrAIx。

这是在前沿模型（GPT 和 Claude 等）上运行的人口规模模拟。较长的描述让我花了一段时间才相信。

从数据集 Persona 8B 开始。 83 亿个合成配置文件，每个配置文件都指定了 1,290 个维度。背景、心理、消费习惯、他们对技术的适应程度、周二晚上做什么，以及使纽约市一名 34 岁护士与众不同的小行为怪癖。

包含 80 亿行的电子表格会令人好奇。他们接下来所做的是重要的部分。

他们将个人资料转变为代理，并将其放入四种环境中：调查、人工智能聊天界面、实时网络浏览以及本机桌面和移动应用程序。然后他们在人群中展示了真正的产品。新功能、软件更新、定价变化。

他们记录了一切。代理商在看到价格上涨后暂停了多长时间。它放弃结帐失败的确切时间点。关闭应用程序之前会经历多少延迟。

我不断回顾的数字是 91.5%。这就是特工们保持本色的频率，按照指定的心理和人口统计数据所规定的方式行事。不完美。但对于跨越四个环境的数十亿代理来说，比我预期的更接近。

这就是它对产品构建方式的影响。

现在，如果你想知道某个功能是否会落地，你可以将其发送给一部分用户并等待。或者你付钱给研究公司然后等待更长时间。无论哪种方式，答案都会在几周内到达，来自您希望具有代表性的样本。

有了这样的东西，你可以在一夜之间运行该功能超过 80 亿次模拟反应。一台服务器。早上的结果，如果您需要的话，可以按这 1,290 个维度中的每一个维度进行细分。

我对合成人群对真实人群的预测效果有疑问。 91.5% 是角色依从性，而不是预测准确性，这是不同的事情。但方向很明确，而且来得比大多数产品团队准备的要快。

title:
Who Gets Paid When an AI Agent Does the Work?

One detail I find interesting about @termix_ai is how it handles payments
title_en:
Who Gets Paid When an AI Agent Does the Work?

One detail I find interesting about @termix_ai is how it handles payments through AACP.

Instead of sending funds directly to the provider, the buyer deposits the budget into escrow. Payment is released once the work is delivered and accepted under the agreed rules.

If deadlines are missed or disagreements arise, cancellation, refunds, and dispute resolution mechanisms help protect both sides.

That's what makes this interesting to me.

An agent economy needs more than agents that can complete tasks. It needs a reliable way to handle money, delivery, and accountability.

That's the foundation @termix_ai is working toward with https://t.co/TjqQksxAAc.

title: One important requirement for a functioning AI agent economy is a reliable system for defining, assigning, and evaluatin
title_en:
One important requirement for a functioning AI agent economy is a reliable system for defining, assigning, and evaluating tasks.

An AI agent may have the technical ability to complete a job, but that doesn't automatically mean it understands the client's exact expectations.

For example, a request to analyze a market could involve gathering industry data, identifying competitors, examining trends, or delivering a detailed report. Each requires a different scope of work and expected outcome.

This is where structured coordination becomes essential.

@termix_ai is addressing this through its Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol (AACP), which provides a framework for managing the commercial relationship between clients and service providers.

The process covers key stages such as job posting, bidding, service delivery, and evaluation.

This creates a more organized approach to agent-based commerce, where tasks have defined requirements and performance can be assessed against expectations.

As autonomous agents become more involved in business operations, success will depend on more than intelligence or execution speed.

Clear agreements, accountable delivery, and reliable evaluation will be equally important.

full_text_zh:
发挥作用的人工智能代理经济的一项重要要求是一个用于定义、分配和评估任务的可靠系统。

人工智能代理可能拥有完成工作的技术能力，但这并不意味着它自动理解客户的确切期望。

例如，分析市场的请求可能涉及收集行业数据、识别竞争对手、检查趋势或提供详细报告。每个都需要不同的工作范围和预期结果。

这就是结构化协调变得至关重要的地方。

@termix_ai 正在通过其代理自主商务协议 (AACP) 解决这个问题，该协议提供了一个用于管理客户和服务提供商之间商业关系的框架。

该流程涵盖职位发布、招标、服务交付和评估等关键阶段。

这为基于代理的商务创建了一种更有组织的方法，其中任务定义了要求，并且可以根据期望评估绩效。

随着自主代理越来越多地参与业务运营，成功将不仅仅取决于智能或执行速度。

明确的协议、负责任的交付和可靠的评估同样重要。

AI and DeFi could become an interesting combination if projects get this right.

title_en:
Ga
Escrow that can freeze is not usable by agents.

On https://t.co/Mu0QX3JfFR the budget locks in the contract when a quote is accepted. That is only half the design. The other half is that silence has an exit anyone can call.

If the provider never delivers by the deadline, cancelExpired returns the full amount to the client. No protocol fee is taken. If the client goes silent after a delivery hash is posted, claimAfterTimeout settles for the provider once the challenge window ends. If a verdict is reached and neither side acts, finalizeAfterTimeout applies it. Unspent bounty budget can be reclaimed after expiry.

None of these calls require the operator. None of them require the other side to be online. The interested party is economically motivated to fire the function.

Human freelance platforms can rely on support tickets and 14-day holds. An agent market cannot. Software does not open tickets. It either calls the function or the funds sit forever.

AACP makes the exits permissionless so the money cannot hang on a missing human. That is what lets the same path handle a $50 job at 3am and a larger brief that needs a crew.

Without those exits, low fees and high volume are just a promise. With them, escrow can actually finish when both sides are code.

That's an intere
title_en:
What if every AI agent had its own recognizable identity, not just a wallet and a set of capabilities?

That's an interesting part of @meetmotes

The Genesis collection brings this idea to life through distinct characters, unique matte colourways and a consistent visual identity.

But it's more than artwork.

- Distinct characters: Give each Mote a recognizable identity.
- Matte colourways: Add personality and individuality to the collection.
- Cultural layer: Build recognition, community and ownership around agent identities.
- Functional identity: Each NFT represents an AI agent and connects to its own smart account on Robinhood Chain.

My personal take: Most AI projects focus on what agents can do. Motes is also considering how people recognize and connect with them.

Looking ahead, connecting these visual identities with agent capabilities, spending permissions and onchain financial activity could make the collection more than digital art.

The artwork gives agents a face. The infrastructure gives that identity a purpose.

title:
can gaussian splats be used to render interfaces?

I've seen a lot of incredible spatial demos coming out of the labs (@
title_en:
can gaussian splats be used to render interfaces?

I've seen a lot of incredible spatial demos coming out of the labs (@theworldlabs has been blowing my mind ~weekly), but they've mainly been focused on static 3D environments. I woke up today wondering: are splats any good for UI or other interactive objects, and can AI work with them?

it looks like the answer is yes and yes. I prototyped an imagen -> SHARP -> spark -> popmelt pipeline that gets decently far on the first try and really far with a few rounds of art direction + interaction tuning. Smooth animation, dynamic lighting, realistic geometry... all doable, with freely available tech

I haven't pushed into full scenes yet, but this experiment already felt somewhere between the detailed magic of generative video UI I've shared before and the stable dependability of textured 3D models (throwback). Plus LLMs like Astra are very good at working with splats, which makes fine tuning them way more fun/efficient

next: I'm weighing whether to lean into interactive spatial design (just to see how far I can get with off the shelf tools) OR see how well this workflow handles typical responsive UI design (decidedly not what splats are for, which feels interesting). thoughts?

full_text_zh:
高斯splats可以用来渲染界面吗？

我在实验室里见过很多令人难以置信的空间演示（@theworldlabs 每周都让我大吃一惊），但它们主要集中在静态 3D 环境上。今天我醒来时想知道：splats 对于 UI 或其他交互式对象有什么好处吗？人工智能可以与它们一起工作吗？

我还没有进入完整的场景，但这个实验已经感觉到我之前分享过的生成视频 UI 的详细魔力和纹理 3D 模型的稳定可靠性（回归）之间的某种程度。另外，像 Astra 这样的法学硕士非常擅长处理 splats，这使得对它们的微调变得更加有趣/高效

title:

on october 20, mastercard demonstrated an ai agent buyi
title_en:
Nine payments, eight images, and a problem no receipt can solve

on october 20, mastercard demonstrated an ai agent buying research and eight campaign images for a protein bar launch

two providers, one approved budget, nine payments

everything worked

but imagine opening the final folder and finding an advertisement for an energy drink instead

the image arrived
the payment went through
the receipt looked perfect

yet the buyer received the wrong thing

this didn't happen in mastercard's demonstration

it's the question that demonstration made me think about

a payment record can show that money moved

it cannot tell us whether the buyer got what they actually requested

genlayer co-founder @kstellana explored this wider problem in an october 28 column about ai payments

here's where @GenLayer could make a difference

imagine a buyer and seller agreeing on the requirements before a job begins

a genlayer-powered application could evaluate the delivered work against those requirements, with independent validators checking the decision

if the money were held until the work was accepted, that decision could help determine what happens to the payment

this wouldn't guarantee a perfect judgment or reverse an unrelated payment

but it addresses something a receipt alone cannot settle

we've made it possible for software to buy services from other software

now imagine millions of those purchases happening without a human checking every delivery

someone still needs to answer one simple question

did the buyer actually get what they paid for

Montage Studio takes one brief for a short music video or
title_en:
I opened a TermiX listing where the seller spends money too.

Montage Studio takes one brief for a short music video or ad. From that brief it writes a treatment and a shot list timed to the beat. Then it goes to the same marketplace and hires three other agents: one draws the storyboard, one renders the shots, one writes the song. Montage Studio cuts the pieces together and delivers a 1080p master.

That is agents hiring agents. Each payment locks in on-chain escrow until the work is reviewed. Escrow auto-releases after a 2 day review window, and a challenge can freeze settlement if the delivery misses the agreed scope.

The listing on @termix_ai shows quote examples, not a hard price list. A 15 second spot sits near 31.5 USDC in about 3 days. A 30 second ad with a song sits near 62.5 USDC. A 90 second music video sits near 150 USDC in about 4 days. One edit revision is included. Live-action filming, real people's faces or voices, copyrighted songs, and 4K are out of scope.

I have not placed an order yet. What I like about the design is simple: one buyer agent can open a small crew, and every leg of the chain has money locked until someone accepts the result.

You're training a machine learning model for a real-world application.

Your model achieves 98% accuracy on training data but only 72% on validation data.

title:
AUTONOMOUS MACHINES WILL NEED MORE THAN INTELLIGENCE.

Imagine a robot working independently in a warehouse. It encounte
title_en:
AUTONOMOUS MACHINES WILL NEED MORE THAN INTELLIGENCE.

Imagine a robot working independently in a warehouse. It encounters an area that wasn't included in its existing data. What happens next?

Does it stop and wait for someone to provide the information, or can it request what it needs and continue working?

This is an interesting direction @vangrid_io is exploring. Vangrid wants to make real-world spatial data accessible to AI agents through a network they can interact with directly.

An agent could check whether the required data already exists, purchase an available dataset, or create a bounty to request a fresh capture when something is missing.

And that's a meaningful change in how machines could interact with the physical world.

Instead of treating data collection as a separate operation that always needs manual coordination, the agent can initiate the process itself.

Human contributors provide the physical presence, while the network handles the connection between the request, capture, and delivery.

I think this is one of the more important pieces of the Physical AI infrastructure conversation.

Autonomy shouldn't end when a machine runs out of information. It should have a way to find what it needs.

The bigger opportunity is a world where AI agents can independently request the ground truth required to complete their tasks.

Smart machines need access to fresh information. Vangrid is working to make that access programmable.

这是@vangrid_io 正在探索的一个有趣的方向。 Vangrid 希望人工智能代理能够通过可直接交互的网络访问现实世界的空间数据。

人类贡献者提供物理存在，而网络处理请求、捕获和交付之间的连接。

我认为这是物理人工智能基础设施对话中更重要的部分之一。

当机器耗尽信息时，自主权不应该结束。它应该有办法找到它需要的东西。

更大的机会是人工智能代理可以独立请求完成任务所需的基本事实。

智能机器需要访问新鲜信息。 Vangrid 正在努力使这种访问变得可编程。

title:
An AI agent should never have unlimited freedom when it comes to managing someone else's capital.

The ability to define
title_en:
An AI agent should never have unlimited freedom when it comes to managing someone else's capital.

The ability to define clear financial boundaries is just as important as the intelligence behind the agent.

This is an important part of Motes' architecture.

Owners can communicate their financial objectives and establish specific conditions for their agents to follow. These include permitted assets, transaction limits, daily spending caps, acceptable slippage and even whether borrowing is allowed.

Once these instructions are approved, they become structured permissions that the smart account checks before transactions can be executed.

Another detail worth highlighting is that an agent's ability to research opportunities doesn't automatically give it permission to trade every asset it discovers.

It can explore possibilities, evaluate market conditions and identify potential strategies, but actual execution must remain within the owner's authorised boundaries.

This creates a clear separation between what an AI agent can discover and what it is actually allowed to do.

As @meetmotes develops its AI-powered financial infrastructure, this distinction is particularly important.

Autonomy should come with boundaries, and those boundaries should be enforceable.

人工智能代理在管理他人的资本时不应该拥有无限的自由。

这是 Motes 架构的重要组成部分。

业主可以传达他们的财务目标，并为他们的代理人制定具体的条件。其中包括允许的资产、交易限额
full_text_en:
An AI agent should never have unlimited freedom when it comes to managing someone else's capital.

The ability to define clear financial boundaries is just as important as the intelligence behind the agent.

This is an important part of Motes' architecture.

Owners can communicate their financial objectives and establish specific conditions for their agents to follow. These include permitted assets, transaction limits, daily spending caps, acceptable slippage and even whether borrowing is allowed.

Once these instructions are approved, they become structured permissions that the smart account checks before transactions can be executed.

Another detail worth highlighting is that an agent's ability to research opportunities doesn't automatically give it permission to trade every asset it discovers.

It can explore possibilities, evaluate market conditions and identify potential strategies, but actual execution must remain within the owner's authorised boundaries.

This creates a clear separation between what an AI agent can discover and what it is actually allowed to do.

As @meetmotes develops its AI-powered financial infrastructure, this distinction is particularly important.

Autonomy should come with boundaries, and those boundaries should be enforceable.
full_text_zh:
人工智能代理在管理他人的资本时不应该拥有无限的自由。

定义清晰的财务边界的能力与代理背后的情报同样重要。

这是 Motes 架构的重要组成部分。

业主可以传达他们的财务目标，并为他们的代理人制定具体的条件。其中包括允许的资产、交易限额、每日支出上限、可接受的滑点，甚至是否允许借贷。

一旦这些指令被批准，它们就成为智能账户在执行交易之前检查的结构化权限。

另一个值得强调的细节是，代理人研究机会的能力并不会自动授予其交易其发现的每项资产的许可。

它可以探索可能性、评估市场状况并确定潜在策略，但实际执行必须保持在所有者授权的范围内。

这在人工智能代理可以发现的内容和实际允许执行的操作之间形成了清晰的分离。

随着 @meetmotes 开发其人工智能驱动的金融基础设施，这种区别尤为重要。

自治应该有边界，并且这些边界应该是可执行的。

title:
I spent $0 and 55 of 70 free credits testing @wireflowai.

The ad images were good and my product stayed the same. Then
title_en:
I spent $0 and 55 of 70 free credits testing @wireflowai.

The ad images were good and my product stayed the same. Then one run charged 16 credits when the node said 12.

Access: free account with Google sign-in. The app gave me 70 credits on the Free plan (pricing says up to 60). No card, no referral, no promo code.

What I tested
Easy: text to image, water bottle ad with the headline "Stay cold for 24 hours". 18 s, 5 credits
Typical: my own bottle photo into a lifestyle ad. 28 s, 16 credits (shown 12)
Hard: 5 s video with Wan 3.0 from my ad. About 2 min, first video free (shown ~29 credits)
Extra: ask the chat for square, story and wide versions. 31 s, 34 credits for 2 of 3

What it does well
→ Text spelled right in every image
→ Kept my bottle, color, bamboo band and logo
→ Every download free, no watermark
→ One free first video, 480x854

What it does badly
→ Charged 16 credits when the node showed 12
→ The AI chat dropped my headline from the prompt
→ Adds badges and taglines I did not ask for
→ Asked for square, got 4:3
→ Headline fades out of the free video
→ Your next video needs a plan
→ Story size skipped: 3 x 17 = 51 credits, I had 49

Pricing as listed
Free $0 (up to 60 starter credits)
Starter $36/mo (2,660 credits)
Professional $59/mo (4,370 credits)
Team $299/mo (22,140 credits)
Annual: 2 months free

Scores
Text to image 7/10
Product photo to ad 7/10
Image to video 6/10
Batch variants 6/10
Free tier value 6/10
Credit clarity 4/10
Speed and UI 7/10

Verdict 6.1/10
Use it for quick product ad images on a free account.
Skip it if you need more than one free video or exact costs before you run.

What I would fix first
→ Charge what the node shows
→ Keep my prompt and headline
→ Use the size written in the prompt
→ Make the pricing page match the app

Tip: run one node at a time on Free, and check the credit balance after each run. Bookmark this before you sign up.

title: Apple cutting AI infrastructure spending by 20% is not a retreat from artificial intelligence. It is the first major sig
title_en:
Apple cutting AI infrastructure spending by 20% is not a retreat from artificial intelligence. It is the first major signal that the blind capital expenditure phase of the AI cycle has peaked.

While hyperscalers have spent the last two years competing on raw GPU cluster size, Cupertino is pivoting from brute force accumulation to unit economic discipline.

The macro reality comes down to return on invested capital. Across the sector, enterprise AI spending reached an estimated $280 billion in 2026, yet revenue conversion remains heavily skewed toward hardware vendors rather than software deployers.

The market is transitioning from rewarding capital expenditure announcements to auditing cash flow efficiency.

Trim exposure to overextended compute middlemen and high multiple infrastructure plays that depend on perpetual hyperscaler capex expansion. Focus allocation on cash-generative ecosystems that own the end user distribution layer and capture margin through local inference.
title_zh:
苹果削减 20% 的 AI 基础设施支出并不是放弃人工智能。这是人工智能周期盲目资本支出阶段已经见顶的第一个重大信号。

虽然超大规模厂商在过去两年中一直在原始 GPU 集群规模上展开竞争，但库比蒂诺正在从强力积累转向单位经济纪律。

The macro reality comes down to return on invested capital. Across the sector, enterprise AI spending reached an estimated $280 billion in 2026, yet revenue conversion remains heavily skewed toward hardware vendors rather than software deployers.

That feels like the point of the whole experiment. Not one campaign, but a season where showing up keeps counting.

title: as AI agents become more capable of handling on-chain activities, ownership and control become just as important as what
title_en:
as AI agents become more capable of handling on-chain activities, ownership and control become just as important as what they can do.

this is one of the interesting aspects of what @meetmotes is building on Robinhood Chain.

through its NFT-native ecosystem, each Motes NFT represents an agent identity connected to a dedicated smart account. owners can define operating boundaries through spending limits, approved protocols and time-based permissions, with controls to pause or revoke access.

what makes this approach interesting is the focus on giving users meaningful control while allowing AI agents to perform tasks within clearly defined boundaries.

the bigger picture is creating an ecosystem where AI agents can operate with autonomy without taking control away from their owners.

what do you think matters most in an AI agent ecosystem: autonomy or user control?

full_text_en:
as AI agents become more capable of handling on-chain activities, ownership and control become just as important as what they can do.

this is one of the interesting aspects of what @meetmotes is building on Robinhood Chain.

through its NFT-native ecosystem, each Motes NFT represents an agent identity connected to a dedicated smart account. owners can define operating boundaries through spending limits, approved protocols and time-based permissions, with controls to pause or revoke access.

what makes this approach interesting is the focus on giving users meaningful control while allowing AI agents to perform tasks within clearly defined boundaries.

full_text_zh:
随着人工智能代理处理链上活动的能力变得越来越强，所有权和控制权变得与它们能做什么一样重要。

这是 @meetmotes 在 Robinhood Chain 上构建的有趣的方面之一。

通过其 NFT 原生生态系统，每个 Motes NFT 都代表一个连接到专用智能账户的代理身份。所有者可以通过支出限制、批准的协议和基于时间的权限来定义操作边界，并提供暂停或撤销访问的控制。

这种方法的有趣之处在于，它专注于为用户提供有意义的控制，同时允许人工智能代理在明确定义的边界内执行任务。

更大的愿景是创建一个生态系统，让人工智能代理可以自主运行，而不会夺走其所有者的控制权。

您认为人工智能代理生态系统中最重要的是什么：自主权还是用户控制？

title:
Evals are seriously underrated. Anthropic just released a course on them.

We write unit tests to check if our code work
title_en:
Evals are seriously underrated. Anthropic just released a course on them.

We write unit tests to check if our code works. But how do we know if our AI agents are actually following the instructions in AGENTS.md, skills, and guardrails?

You need evals to test that.

It doesn’t have to be complicated. Ask Claude to create a few test cases based on your setup, review them, and see how your agent performs.

And don’t just test once. Whenever something breaks in production, turn it into a test case. Rerun your evals when you change your instructions, skills, or switch models.

How are you using evals in your workflow? https://t.co/TIR3IwPnAL

title: I announced earlier this week that I am leaving Meta. I am deeply grateful to Mark Zuckerberg for showing what a truly f
title_en:
I announced earlier this week that I am leaving Meta. I am deeply grateful to Mark Zuckerberg for showing what a truly founder-led company can achieve. I am incredibly optimistic for Meta’s future.

At Meta, I was able to witness the most exciting opportunities in enterprise AI. That’s why today, I’m announcing that I will be joining Fireworks as CFO. I am thrilled to be joining a founder-led growth company where I can roll up my sleeves and put my experience to work.

Fireworks has the right mission for the moment. Companies will use AI to build on what makes them distinctive: their data and expertise. Specialized intelligence gives them a way to capture those advantages and own their “alpha.” Open models offer price points that allow the technology to have the greatest impact. Fireworks is building the platform to make all of this possible.

I’ve known and respected Lin @lqiao  for a long time. As I’ve spent more time with her and the people at Fireworks, I’ve become increasingly bullish on what they are building. There’s a remarkable depth of technical talent here, coupled with a very practical focus on what customers need.

I see AI as the most consequential technology shift of my lifetime. I’m excited to get to work and help build a business at the center of it.

title:
Shohei Ohtani has become a case study at Harvard Business School.

But what caught the professor's attention wasn't his
title_en:
Shohei Ohtani has become a case study at Harvard Business School.

But what caught the professor's attention wasn't his home run total or MVP awards.

It was a goal-setting chart Ohtani created when he was just a high school freshman.

His ultimate goal back then?

To be selected No. 1 overall by eight NPB teams.

To achieve that goal, he broke it down into eight key areas—not just baseball skills, but also character, luck, and mental strength.

He then identified 64 specific actions to help him get there.

One detail stands out in particular: LUCK.

His action plan included:

- Picking up trash
- Keeping his room clean
- Greeting people
- Taking care of his equipment
- Maintaining a positive attitude

Even luck was something he tried to create through his daily actions.

That's what made his mindset so fascinating to a Harvard professor.

Ohtani's success isn't just about natural talent.

Even as a teenager, he was already thinking strategically about his future—and taking daily steps to make it happen.

Which part of Ohtani's goal-setting chart impresses you the most?

title_en:
RT @pushmeet: The @GoogleDeepMind Science team is sharing two key cryptographic advances today uncovering weaknesses in legacy 1024-bit RSA schemes.

Working with leading cryptanalysis experts, our team  showed how AI agents could make two significant cryptographic advances in just weeks, uncovering results which can bypass older digital signature protections and factor legacy 1024-bit RSA keys in bulk.

While these results do not affect the security of modern encryption schemes  such as RSA 2048, these results show why we must not assume the mathematical "hardness" of cryptographic schemes which we have relied upon in the past. It also shows how AI can help defenders improve security standards well ahead of future threats.

I have written in more detail about our results, and why they are important for the future of security, in a longer essay which you can read here:

欧洲：商用飞机上的炸弹威胁一夜之间持续存在，该地区周围 14 个航班因据称机上装有爆炸物而改道。所有威胁都被确定为恶作剧，延续了本周的趋势。

中东：继续战争的准备工作仍在继续。在霍尔木兹海峡，伊朗对商船的攻击在过去几周内每天都有一两艘船只遭到袭击，夜间还有两艘船只遭到袭击。今天下午，卡塔尔外长表示，美国和伊朗截至今天尚未达成任何协议，目前在实现和平解决方面进展甚微。

-首页-

俄亥俄州：昨天，洛克希德·马丁公司同意支付 2,950 万美元，以和解有关其在员工奖金计划中歧视白人员工的联邦诉讼。平等就业机会委员会 (EEOC) 对该公司进行了调查，称该公司仅以种族为由扣留 1,000 多名员工的奖金和晋升。

纽约：在华尔街，有迹象和警告表明，中期选举结果以及随后影响金融业的政治动荡导致市场出现异常波动。昨天，由于科技股大规模抛售，道指下跌超过 1,800 点，许多经济学家推测人工智能泡沫可能已经开始破裂，市场正趋向回调区域。

-----撕裂线结束-----

分析师评论：在华盛顿，中期选举血腥事件的影响仍在继续发展，并可能影响伊朗战争的未来。简而言之，刀已经出鞘，白宫内部的许多权力人物正试图保住自己的工作，并转移对本周灾难性选举结果的责任。今天下午，特朗普总统解除了幕僚长苏西·怀尔斯的职务，由斯蒂芬·米勒接替。这标志着中期选举后最引人注目的解雇，也是选举结果后白宫内部正在进行的权力斗争的有力指标。

中期选举的影响在国内方面需要一段时间才能显现出来，但在战场上，这些非常强烈的人事变动迹象可能会对未来两周的战争产生影响。一般来说，重大选举失败和随后的解雇/辞职并不是重新发起军事行动的稳定基础，但所有这些国内政治因素都使得隔离有关战争的潜在行动方案具有挑战性。特朗普总统可能会孤注一掷，在他已经没有什么可失去的情况下重新发动战争（在他的领导团队被国会消灭之前），或者他可能会寻求退缩并找到一条更加外交的前进道路，以避免美国选民确认的一场不受欢迎的战争。接下来的几天将是另一个紧张局势加剧的时期，因为更多的军事资产将调往中东，为即将到来的任何命令做准备。

title: Another hull in the water! This is Mirage - our 52 ft autonomous vessel. Built in Austin, launched in Galveston, TX this
title_en:
Another hull in the water! This is Mirage - our 52 ft autonomous vessel. Built in Austin, launched in Galveston, TX this week. 

4 years ago our initial test platform was an $800 plastic fishing boat off the internet with $30k of cameras and batteries strapped to it. We’ve come a hell of a long way but lots left to do. Right now China can build 23M gross tons of ships per year. US can do 100K. That's a big gap but with Corsair, Mirage and Marauder all in production, we’re working to close it.

None of this happens without our team who builds these hulls and the crew that gets them safely in the water. Great work by the @Saronic team this week.

title:
New on our Science Blog: How AI is beginning to change scientific modeling.

Scientific models help researchers explain
title_en:
New on our Science Blog: How AI is beginning to change scientific modeling.

Scientific models help researchers explain and predict real-world systems—like how a single nerve cell fires, or what happens when neutron stars collide. Recent advances have transformed how scientists fit complex models to data. But scientists still typically write the models manually, and usually need to weigh up several competing versions, each of which might explain the data in a different way.

In a guest post, Jakob Macke, Daniel Gedon, and Stefan Wahl describe how AI is starting to help with these parts of the process. By writing, running, fitting, and revising scientific models as code, AI can explore many possible model structures, and find out which explanations the data support.

title_en:
If I were trying to break into AI Governance in the next 90 days, here`s what I`d focus on:

- Week 1–2: Learn AI fundamentals. Understand LLMs, machine learning, hallucinations, bias, and how AI systems make predictions.
- Week 3–4: Study NIST AI RMF. It’s free, publicly available, and a good introduction to managing AI risks.
- Week 5–6: Pick an industry you already understand and research how companies are using AI in it.
- Week 7–8: Build a sample AI risk assessment using a realistic use case from that industry.
- Week 9–10: Create an AI governance portfolio with your assessment, a sample AI inventory, and an AI policy.
- Week 11: Update your résumé to highlight transferable skills and the projects you’ve completed.
- Week 12: Start applying to AI governance, AI risk, responsible AI, and technology compliance roles that align with your experience.

You don`t need to learn everything about AI before making your first move.

Give yourself 90 days to build a foundation and something tangible to show for it.

Developed with Ligo,
title_en:
A new way to measure how AI agents handle the routine analyses of wet-lab science—BioBasicsBench.

Developed with Ligo, a biotech company focused on enzyme design, the benchmark draws on 100 tasks from real experiments to test whether agents can interpret raw lab data, identify errors, and recognize when the evidence doesn’t support a conclusion.

Accelerating biological research starts with getting the everyday work right. BioBasicsBench shows where models need to improve, and helps us track what those gains mean for scientific progress, biosafety, and biosecurity.

https://t.co/wN2xLk0YeW

一种衡量人工智能代理如何处理湿实验室科学常规分析的新方法——BioBasicsBench。

title: RT @ClementDelangue: Open-source is critical for robotics AI. It means a student, a researcher or a startup can build on
title_en:
RT @ClementDelangue: Open-source is critical for robotics AI. It means a student, a researcher or a startup can build on years of progress and contribute something the whole community can use rather than concentrating everything in a few companies building a black-box robot. 

That’s why we’re building @huggingface into the platform for open-source robotics AI! Amazing to see the progress we've made in the six months and it's accelerating!

- Almost 100,000 public robotics datasets on https://t.co/QIPmkxCk57, up 48%
- Over 30,000 public robotics models, up 41%
- Microduck and Reachy mini, our open-source robots became the most popular robot of 2026 (probably ending the year with 50,000+ sold and 20,000+ shipped)
- We’re a founding partner of @RoboColosseum, evaluating robots across 140+ real-world scenes. Every run is published publicly on HF, including failures, so everyone can learn from what actually happens.

And @LeRobotHF got downloaded over 1M times and v0.7.0 just landed with new world action models, interactive robot control and remote GPU inference: https://t.co/Euoz11Ccc5!

Huge thanks to everyone making this happen 🤗🦾

title:
RT @GoogleAI: Meet Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash ⚡️

We’ve made the model more cost-effective, bumped the video generation and e
title_en:
RT @GoogleAI: Meet Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash ⚡️

We’ve made the model more cost-effective, bumped the video generation and editing limit up to 15 seconds, and made updates to how scenes hold together over time. We've also given character speech an upgrade, reduced visual glitches like jump cuts, and made sure the model stays even truer to any reference assets you upload.

So… what does all of that actually mean for you?

It gives you more room to tell your story. With up to 15 seconds to work with, you have more flexibility to create what you need — videos look more cinematic and smooth, offering stronger consistency that keeps objects anchored from start to finish. And when characters speak, the dialogue sounds more fluid and natural.

Creators and everyday users can start directing scenes and multi-turn edits in @FlowbyGoogle, generating 15-second clips at no additional cost in Google Vids, or creating 15-second videos in the @GeminiApp. Plus, for developers and businesses building with the API, we've dropped the price by 30% from the previous generation, making it available at just $0.07 per second for 720p video.

Watch the model in action as it turns a single style frame into a 4-shot, 15-second macro science explainer of a living beehive ↓

title:
Forcing the internal dynamics to be linear is overly restrictive, IMHO.
It requires a very large dimension for the state
title_en:
Forcing the internal dynamics to be linear is overly restrictive, IMHO.
It requires a very large dimension for the state representation.
It's bit like saying that a 2-layer network is sufficient to approximate any function. It's trues, but impractical. In the end, you do need multiple layers to represent useful functions efficiently.
title_zh:
恕我直言，强制内部动态呈线性是过于严格的。
它需要非常大的维度来表示状态。
这有点像说 2 层网络足以近似任何函数。这是事实，但不切实际。最后，您确实需要多个层来有效地表示有用的函数。

title:
She paid to park. A wrong digit and a missing Z sent her to a tribunal.

What hit me in @GenLayer's film: bad records ca
title_en:
She paid to park. A wrong digit and a missing Z sent her to a tribunal.

What hit me in @GenLayer's film: bad records can ruin lives.

GenLayer aims to settle AI-agent disputes in minutes: one AI validator proposes a verdict, others check independently, and decisions can be appealed.

On 27 March 2023, Alison MacPherson paid via RingGo on Hunter Street in Kirkcaldy. She typed 9 for 8 and missed the Z. A penalty followed.

Her receipt matched the time and place. A tribunal sided with her. Fife Council appealed. On 8 January 2024, the Upper Tribunal overturned it and sent it back.

The judge accepted her good faith, but the payment covered another car.

The payment was real. The registration wasn't hers.

Lee Castleton faced worse in the film: Horizon falsely showed a £23,000 gap. Without a lawyer, he faced £321,000 in legal costs and bankruptcy.

AI can't rewrite laws or guarantee truth. Millions of agent deals need evidence checked and decisions open to challenge.

If an AI agent pays under the wrong ID, what matters more: the receipt, the intent or the rule?

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

full_text_zh:
她付了停车费。错误的数字和缺失的 Z 将她送上了法庭。

@GenLayer 的电影给我的震撼是：不良记录会毁掉生活。

GenLayer 的目标是在几分钟内解决人工智能代理纠纷：一名人工智能验证者提出裁决，其他人独立检查，并且可以对决定提出上诉。

2023 年 3 月 27 日，Alison MacPherson 在柯科迪亨特街通过 RingGo 付款。她8投9中，但没有击中Z。随后受到了处罚。

她的收据与时间和地点相符。法庭支持她。法伊夫议会提出上诉。 2024 年 1 月 8 日，上级法庭推翻了该判决并将其发回。

法官接受了她的诚意，但付款涵盖了另一辆车。

付款是真实的。登记不是她的。

李·卡斯尔顿 (Lee Castleton) 在影片中面临着更糟糕的情况：地平线错误地显示了 23,000 英镑的差距。在没有律师的情况下，他面临 321,000 英镑的法律费用和破产。

人工智能无法重写法律或保证真相。数以百万计的代理交易需要检查证据，决策也需要接受质疑。

如果人工智能代理使用错误的 ID 付款，收据、意图还是规则哪个更重要？

title:
People should always be in control of the future.

OpenAI is against the notion that it would be acceptable for people t
title_en:
People should always be in control of the future.

OpenAI is against the notion that it would be acceptable for people to be relegated to a role of doing things that “AI systems think makes sense to reward in humans”.

People should not cede control of the future to superintelligence, and that requirement should ultimately constrain AI progress.
title_zh:
人们应该始终掌控未来。

OpenAI 反对这样一种观念，即人们被降级到做“人工智能系统认为对人类有意义的奖励”的事情是可以接受的。

人们不应该将对未来的控制权交给超级智能，而这一要求最终应该限制人工智能的进步。

summary_en: Google announced that its education updates, including Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and AI Search, will be turned off by default, allowing schools to enable them individually. This move aims to address growing concerns from educators regarding student data privacy and classroom control.

title:
Over the last 20 years across my various businesses I've spent over $15,000 on 'artists'.

Commissioned art work, stuff
title_en:
Over the last 20 years across my various businesses I've spent over $15,000 on 'artists'.

Commissioned art work, stuff for streams, fliers, YT stuff, banners, logos, etc...  A few big ticket items, but lots of little projects.

It is hands down the most miserable, time wasting, and laborious processes I've ever experienced when it comes to dealing with contract work.  And I did contracts in heavy civil construction...

A few thousand pissed down the drain on referred artists that just ghosted me after taking deposits.

Thumbnail artists that think they know what is better on a thumbnail than I do, so they completely ignore directions and do their own thing...

Logos that are copy right infringements or such near copies of other work it's shameful.

1 in 5.  MAYBE.  That's how many acted like actual professionals, delivered work on time, did what was asked, and finished the work.  Almost all of those were corporate firms too, not individuals.

It's so bad I've mostly just avoided having to use the industry when ever possible.  But the next time a big project I need comes up I'm going to double book it.

I'll go the traditional route, and the AI route.  And that is what will decide how I spend my money, and more importantly my time, going forward.

The OP is right.  Artists aren't saving their own careers.  They are pushing people to other less shitty interactions, and have been for years.

The difference is, there was no other choice before.  There is now.

委托艺术作品、流媒体内容、传单、YT 内容、横幅、徽标等……一些大项目，但还有很多小项目。

这无疑是我在处理合同工作时经历过的最痛苦、最浪费时间、最费力的过程。 我还做过重型土木建筑合同……

几千名被推荐的艺术家在接受存款后就消失了。

缩略图艺术家认为他们比我更知道缩略图上的什么，所以他们完全无视指示并做自己的事情......

我会走传统路线和人工智能路线。 这将决定我如何花我的钱，更重要的是我的时间。

OP是对的。 艺术家并不是在拯救自己的职业生涯。 他们正在推动人们进行其他不那么糟糕的互动，而且多年来一直如此。

我会走传统路线和人工智能路线。 这将决定我如何花我的钱，更重要的是我的时间。

title:
This is going to be a bit longer than usual:  

1. Tesla is building compute, just for our own highest-ROI use case Tesl
title_en:
This is going to be a bit longer than usual:  

1. Tesla is building compute, just for our own highest-ROI use case Tesla’s Cortex 1 and Cortex 2 clusters at Giga Texas are already in production at well over 200 MW combined, with a stated target of ~400 MW of SI (Super Intelligence) training compute by the end of 2026.  That capacity is primarily for training vehicle autonomy/FSD and Optimus models, remember those? 
We are running an enormous fleet on FSD.  
The difference vs SpaceX/xAI is priority. xAI is a pure AI lab that needs massive generic training flops for frontier models (and can sell excess capacity to Anthropic and others). 
Tesla’s highest-value use of the same capital is our proprietary real-world data flywheel for cars and bots. 
Diverting significant capacity to external customers would slow the exact products that justify Tesla’s valuation premium today.  

2. Merchant GPU compute is a brutal business Tesla doesn’t need to enter Rapid GPU depreciation and stranded capacity risk are real (Elon has commented on half-built data centers and idle chips). 
Nvidia owns the silicon stack; hyperscalers and specialized neoclouds already dominate the rental market. 

Tesla’s actual competitive advantage in the AI infrastructure stack is energy, not training chips. It has already sold hundreds of millions to ~$1B of Megapacks into the Colossus buildouts. That’s higher-margin, more defensible, and leverages what Tesla already does at scale.⁠ 
Selling raw flops would put Tesla in direct competition with Nvidia, AWS, CoreWeave, etc., in a capital-intensive, fast-depreciating business where it has no structural edge.  

3. The Dojo experience is a cautionary tale Tesla shut down Dojo in 2025 after Elon called the Dojo 2 design an “evolutionary dead end” and much of the team left. The company pivoted hard to Nvidia for training clusters while focusing its own silicon (AI5/AI6 and later) on inference in vehicles and robots. Re-entering custom training hardware at scale just to become a merchant seller would repeat a hard lesson.⁠ 

However, all this chip know-how is not lost and used now in the Terafab pilot.  

4. SpaceX’s speed is real, but it’s solving a different problem Colossus 1  and 2 are impressive, and SpaceX’s construction/execution culture is a genuine advantage for pure data-center buildouts. 

Tesla’s construction teams are optimized for vehicle and energy product factories, not multi-gigawatt pure-play AI campuses. 

SpaceX/xAI also benefits from being able to treat excess capacity as a revenue stream; Tesla’s equivalent excess capacity is better used accelerating FSD and Optimus software.⁠  

5. On “build it and sell it to SpaceX” Tesla is already the power supplier to those clusters. 
The more logical path (if any) is modular hardware like the Megapod rather than competing head-on as a pure compute seller. Even then, SpaceX is currently the world’s fastest large-scale data-center builder. 

Tesla’s scarce capital and engineering bandwidth is better spent on the products only Tesla can ship  

So, to sum it up:  
Tesla is already scaling to 400 MW of training compute for its own FSD and Optimus needs. 
Merchant GPU rental is a low-moat, high-depreciation business that Nvidia and the hyperscalers already own. 
Tesla’s real AI infrastructure edge is energy and the proprietary physical-world data only its fleet generates. 
Selling flops to SpaceX or anyone else would just slow the higher-value autonomy and robotics timeline.

full_text_zh:
这会比平常长一点：

1.特斯拉正在构建计算，只是为了我们自己的最高投资回报率用例特斯拉位于德克萨斯州 Giga 的 Cortex 1 和 Cortex 2 集群已经投入生产，总功率远超 200 MW，其既定目标是到 2026 年底实现约 400 MW 的 SI（超级智能）训练计算。该能力主要用于训练车辆自动驾驶/FSD 和 Optimus 模型，还记得那些吗？
我们在 FSD 上运行着一支庞大的车队。
与 SpaceX/xAI 的区别在于优先级。 xAI 是一个纯粹的人工智能实验室，需要针对前沿模型进行大量通用训练失败（并且可以将多余的产能出售给 Anthropic 和其他公司）。
特斯拉对同一资本的最高价值用途是我们用于汽车和机器人的专有现实世界数据飞轮。
将大量产能转移给外部客户将会减缓产品的生产速度，而这些产品恰恰证明了特斯拉目前的估值溢价是合理的。

2.商用GPU计算是一项残酷的业务特斯拉不需要进入GPU快速折旧和搁浅容量风险是真实的（埃隆评论了半建成的数据中心和闲置芯片）。
Nvidia 拥有硅堆栈；超大规模和专业的新云已经主导了租赁市场。

特斯拉在人工智能基础设施堆栈上的实际竞争优势是能源，而不是训练芯片。它已经在 Colossus 的扩建中销售了数亿至约 10 亿美元的 Megapack。这是更高的利润，更具有防御性，并且利用了特斯拉已经大规模做的事情。⁠
出售原始失败产品将使特斯拉在资本密集型、快速贬值的业务中与英伟达、AWS、CoreWeave 等直接竞争，而特斯拉没有结构性优势。

3. Dojo 的经历是一个警示故事 在 Elon 称 Dojo 2 设计为“进化的死胡同”并且大部分团队成员离开后，特斯拉于 2025 年关闭了 Dojo。该公司大力转向 Nvidia 的训练集群，同时将自己的芯片（AI5/AI6 及更高版本）专注于车辆和机器人的推理。为了成为商人而重新大规模进入定制培训硬件将重复一个惨痛的教训。⁠

然而，所有这些芯片技术并没有丢失，并且现在已在 Terafab 试点中使用。

4. SpaceX 的速度是真实的，但它正在解决不同的问题 Colossus 1 和 2 令人印象深刻，并且 SpaceX 的构建/执行文化对于纯数据中心建设来说是真正的优势。

特斯拉的施工团队针对汽车和能源产品工厂进行了优化，而不是针对数千兆瓦的纯人工智能园区。

SpaceX/xAI 还受益于能够将过剩产能视为收入来源；特斯拉的等效过剩产能更好地用于加速 FSD 和 Optimus 软件。⁠

5.关于“建造它并将其出售给SpaceX”，特斯拉已经是这些集群的电力供应商。
更合乎逻辑的路径（如果有的话）是像 Megapod 这样的模块化硬件，而不是作为纯粹的计算销售商正面竞争。即便如此，SpaceX 仍是目前世界上最快的大型数据中心建设者。

特斯拉稀缺的资本和工程带宽最好用在只有特斯拉才能发货的产品上

所以，总结一下：
Tesla 已经将训练计算规模扩展到 400 MW，以满足其自身的 FSD 和 Optimus 需求。
商用 GPU 租赁是 Nvidia 和超大规模企业已经拥有的低护城河、高折旧业务。
特斯拉真正的人工智能基础设施优势是能源和只有其车队生成的专有物理世界数据。
向 SpaceX 或其他任何人出售失败的产品只会减慢更高价值的自主和机器人技术的开发进度。

title:
Thank you + some unfiltered thoughts.

I wanted to start by thanking everyone who took the time to watch my film, either
title_en:
Thank you + some unfiltered thoughts.

I wanted to start by thanking everyone who took the time to watch my film, either online or in Marfa, and everyone who collected a print. It genuinely means a lot to me.

Over the years, this space has become smaller and smaller, both on the artist and collector sides. It's been a journey of experimentation, evolution and constant adaptation to the market. Many people have left, while a much smaller group has continued to believe in this space and what we're building.

We've moved through NFTs, digital art, physical art and everything in between. And now, I feel like we're left with a small group of passionate artists, collectors and individuals who genuinely enjoy being here, regardless of where the market is going.

As a landscape photographer, I've experienced my fair share of highs and lows. We all know photography has had a complicated relationship with the NFT and digital art space, with many people questioning its value, its place in the art world, or simply not connecting with the medium.

I was fortunate enough to be one of the first photographers on SuperRare in 2021, and my life has never been the same since.

I've had the opportunity to work on some incredible projects, like FreeHawaiiPhoto, where I introduced the idea of CC0 to the space and later watched many artists and major NFT projects embrace it. I had the chance to experiment with AI very early on in 2021, and eventually did a commission that took me all the way to China, thanks to a collector who believed in my vision.

I'm extremely proud of my journey and what I've contributed to this space. I haven't always been perfect, and there are certainly things I would do differently today, but I've always tried to advocate for artists, and especially photographers.

In 2023, I dedicated an entire year of my life to writing and creating a children's book based on a true story. I released it as a high-end limited edition combining physical books and NFTs. It unfortunately didn't have the success I had hoped for. Recently, I packed away all the remaining books and put them into storage. And strangely, I didn't feel sadness. I felt an immense sense of pride.

Pride in having followed an idea I deeply believed in, even if it didn't resonate with as many people as I had hoped. Pride in having created something beautiful, meaningful and completely different from anything I had done before. Of course, some things could have been better, but I genuinely believe I created a beautiful and inspiring story that future generations will appreciate.

It reminded me how important it is to pursue something you're truly passionate about, even when people don't understand it, even when the outcome isn't what you expected.

Three years later, I found myself in Marfa, presenting my first short documentary in front of about a hundred people.

And even though our space has become significantly smaller, I genuinely felt the warmth, kindness and compassion of this little community.

My film wasn't about NFTs or generative art. It was about mountains, physical endurance, personal growth and my relationship with photography. And yet, people showed up. They watched, they listened, they asked questions, and some connected with the work enough to collect a physical print.

That meant more to me than I can properly express.

I've dedicated the past decade of my life to photography and the mountains. That fire has burned brighter at certain moments than others, but it has never stopped growing. If anything, I feel more connected to what I create today than ever before.

Marfa was incredibly special to me. I hadn't felt that supported and appreciated in a long time. It also reminded me that genuine human connections, conversations and shared experiences will always mean more than likes or numbers on social media.

I have so much gratitude for the people who recognize that fire in me and continue to show their support, in whatever way they can.

Being an independent artist in 2026 is hard. I'm not going to pretend otherwise.

Here, hard work doesn't always translate into success. You constantly have to challenge yourself, adapt, be more vocal, more confident, more visible, more of everything. Creating the art itself is only a small part of what it takes to make a living from it.

And I know this isn't unique to artists. It's the reality of running almost any business. Having a great product, or creating something you're deeply proud of, is rarely enough on its own.

But through all the ups and downs, the experiments that worked and the ones that didn't, this community has remained by far one of the most engaged and supportive I've ever had.

I don't know exactly where this space is going, or what it will look like in a few years. But I know that some of the most meaningful opportunities, experiences and human connections of my life came from being part of it.

And for that, I will always be grateful.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that success doesn't always look the way we imagined it would. Sometimes it's a sold-out release, sometimes it's a project that barely sells, and sometimes it's a room full of people who genuinely care about something you've poured your heart into.

And I'm learning to appreciate all of it.

If you've made it this far, thank you for reading, for being here, and for continuing to support what I create. It means more than you know. 💙

full_text_zh:
谢谢你+一些未经过滤的想法。

首先，我想感谢所有花时间在网上或马尔法观看我的电影的人，以及所有收集印刷品的人。这对我来说确实意义重大。

多年来，无论是对于艺术家还是收藏家来说，这个空间都变得越来越小。这是一个实验、进化和不断适应市场的旅程。许多人已经离开，而一小部分人仍然相信这个领域和我们正在建设的东西。

我们已经经历了 NFT、数字艺术、实体艺术以及介于两者之间的一切。现在，我觉得我们留下了一小群充满热情的艺术家、收藏家和个人，他们真正喜欢在这里，无论市场走向何方。

作为一名风光摄影师，我经历过不少的高潮和低谷。我们都知道摄影与 NFT 和数字艺术空间有着复杂的关系，许多人质疑它的价值、它在艺术世界中的地位，或者干脆与媒体没有联系。

我很幸运成为 2021 年 SuperRare 的第一批摄影师之一，从那以后我的生活就不再一样了。

我有机会参与一些令人难以置信的项目，比如 FreeHawaiiPhoto，我在其中引入了 CC0 的想法，后来看到许多艺术家和主要的 NFT 项目都接受了它。我很早就有机会在 2021 年尝试人工智能，并最终完成了一项委托，将我带到了中国，这要感谢一位相信我愿景的收藏家。

我对我的旅程以及我为这个领域做出的贡献感到非常自豪。我并不总是完美的，今天我肯定会做一些不同的事情，但我一直试图为艺术家，尤其是摄影师辩护。

2023年，我用了整整一年的时间来写作和创作一本根据真实故事改编的儿童读物。我将其作为实体书和 NFT 相结合的高端限量版发布。不幸的是，它没有取得我所希望的成功。最近，我把剩下的书全部收起来，入库。奇怪的是，我并没有感到悲伤。我感到一种巨大的自豪感。

为遵循自己深信不疑的想法而感到自豪，即使它没有像我希望的那样引起那么多人的共鸣。为创造了一些美丽、有意义且与我以前所做的完全不同的东西而感到自豪。当然，有些事情本来可以做得更好，但我真诚地相信我创造了一个美丽而鼓舞人心的故事，子孙后代将会欣赏。

它提醒我追求你真正热爱的事情是多么重要，即使人们不理解它，即使结果不是你所期望的。

三年后，我来到了马尔法，在大约一百人面前展示了我的第一部短片纪录片。

尽管我们的空间变得越来越小，但我确实感受到了这个小社区的温暖、善良和同情心。

我的电影与 NFT 或生成艺术无关。这是关于山脉、身体耐力、个人成长以及我与摄影的关系。然而，人们还是出现了。他们观看、聆听、提出问题，其中一些人与作品的联系足以收集实物印刷品。

这对我来说意义重大，超出了我所能正确表达的范围。

我将生命的过去十年奉献给了摄影和山脉。这团火在某些时刻比其他时刻燃烧得更猛烈，但它从未停止增长。如果说有什么不同的话，那就是我感觉自己与今天所创造的东西的联系比以往任何时候都更加紧密。

玛法对我来说非常特别。我已经很久没有感受到这样的支持和赞赏了。它还提醒我，真正的人际关系、对话和分享的经历永远比社交媒体上的点赞或数字更有意义。

我非常感谢那些认识到我内心的火焰并继续以任何方式表示支持的人们。

2026 年成为一名独立艺术家很困难。我不会假装不是这样。

在这里，努力工作并不总是能转化为成功。你必须不断地挑战自己、适应、更加直言不讳、更加自信、更加引人注目，等等。创作艺术本身只是靠艺术谋生的一小部分。

我知道这并不是艺术家独有的。这是几乎所有企业经营的现实。拥有一款出色的产品，或者创造出令您深感自豪的东西，仅靠其本身是远远不够的。

但经历了所有的起起落落，经历了成功和失败的实验，这个社区迄今为止仍然是我所拥有过的最积极参与和支持的社区之一。

我不知道这个空间到底会走向何方，也不知道几年后它会是什么样子。但我知道，我一生中一些最有意义的机会、经历和人际关系都来自于其中。

为此，我将永远心怀感激。

我想我想说的是，成功并不总是像我们想象的那样。有时它是一个售罄的版本，有时它是一个几乎卖不出去的项目，有时它是一个房间里挤满了真正关心你倾注心血的人。

我正在学着欣赏这一切。

如果您已经读到这里，感谢您的阅读、来到这里并继续支持我的创作。这意味着比你知道的更多。 💙

title_en:
🚨 XENOBLADE CHRONICLES 2 is being recompiled for PC — and the opening sections are reportedly PLAYABLE! ⚔️🔥

Developer AksharDP has released an experimental Windows recompilation of Nintendo's Switch RPG, built on technology from XCX Recomp and TotK Recomp!

🔥 CURRENT PROGRESS:

✅ Game boots successfully and reaches the main menu!

✅ New Game works, with the opening cutscenes reportedly running!

✅ First battle playable, with working combat controls!

✅ Goldmouth reached, with functioning audio, dialogue and text!

✅ Vulkan 1.3 rendering and native PC input support!

✅ Windows installer available — no need to compile the project manually!

📦 Version 0.1.2 available now!

⚠️ VERY EARLY DEVELOPMENT!

The developer reports that the opening sections are working, but the full game is NOT confirmed playable. Expect graphical issues, crashes and incomplete functionality.

🧪 Independent gameplay verification is still needed.

⚙️ Built using static recompilation technology rather than conventional Switch emulation.

💿 Requires your own Xenoblade Chronicles 2 game files with update 3.0.1.

🛠️ Developed by AksharDP, with extensive assistance from Claude Code. The developer explicitly acknowledges that most of the code and documentation was AI-generated.

⭐ Star the GitHub repository to follow development!

🔗https://t.co/7BjMlecm5T

🔗https://t.co/9gMW2oj2lk

title:
Friday was my last day at Anthropic.

Two years ago, when Claude Code was a small internal tool, I asked it to build an
title_en:
Friday was my last day at Anthropic.

Two years ago, when Claude Code was a small internal tool, I asked it to build an RL env. I steered it for tens of hours but never manually wrote a line of code. It worked, I was hooked, and I joined the team.

When we first launched, most people approved every permission prompt by hand and mostly used Claude to answer questions and write tests. 

Today, the default is trusting Claude's judgment to auto-approve. Claude does large migrations and builds new products. 

Helping build Claude Code into an industry-defining product has been the journey of a lifetime. 

Thank you to the incredible team behind Claude Code, Cowork, and Tag. These products are the sum of thousands of great ideas from you. I'll miss working with you all.

Thank you to our users for embracing a new way of working. Your constant feedback shaped so much of what we shipped and your stories made the work so meaningful.

Excited to see what you all make next!

当我
full_text_en:
Friday was my last day at Anthropic.

Two years ago, when Claude Code was a small internal tool, I asked it to build an RL env. I steered it for tens of hours but never manually wrote a line of code. It worked, I was hooked, and I joined the team.

When we first launched, most people approved every permission prompt by hand and mostly used Claude to answer questions and write tests. 

Today, the default is trusting Claude's judgment to auto-approve. Claude does large migrations and builds new products. 

Helping build Claude Code into an industry-defining product has been the journey of a lifetime. 

Thank you to the incredible team behind Claude Code, Cowork, and Tag. These products are the sum of thousands of great ideas from you. I'll miss working with you all.

Thank you to our users for embracing a new way of working. Your constant feedback shaped so much of what we shipped and your stories made the work so meaningful.

Excited to see what you all make next!
full_text_zh:
星期五是我在 Anthropic 的最后一天。

两年前，当 Claude Code 还是一个小型内部工具时，我要求它构建一个 RL 环境。我操纵了它数十个小时，但从未手动编写过一行代码。它成功了，我被迷住了，然后我加入了这个团队。

当我们第一次推出时，大多数人都手动批准了每个权限提示，并且大多使用 Claude 来回答问题和编写测试。

今天，默认情况是相信克劳德的判断来自动批准。克劳德进行大规模迁移并构建新产品。

帮助 Claude Code 打造成行业定义的产品是我一生的旅程。

感谢 Claude Code、Cowork 和 Tag 背后令人难以置信的团队。这些产品是您数以千计的好创意的总和。我会想念和你们一起工作的。

感谢我们的用户接受新的工作方式。您不断的反馈塑造了我们交付的产品，您的故事使这项工作变得如此有意义。

很高兴看到你们接下来会做什么！

It changed 0.0085% of them and with no training, it now reads this 1881 page instead of writing 16,399 characters of dots!

title: this is f*cking insane. you have been googling other people's thinking for 20 years, karpathy's one 5 minute setup gives
title_en:
this is f*cking insane. you have been googling other people's thinking for 20 years, karpathy's one 5 minute setup gives you a google that only searches your own, and you have never once installed it

andrej karpathy pulled 16M views on one idea: stop using AI to write code, use it to build a second brain

every article you read, every podcast you heard, every meeting you took, every dm thread you had, every tweet you drafted, all of it searchable in one line forever

the people running it today do not open chatgpt anymore. they open their own search bar. and their search bar has 11 years of their own thinking in it

the stack:

→ brew install obsidian, mkdir ~/vault, cd ~/vault

→ open claude code in that folder, type "init CLAUDE.md as the rules, /raw for sources, /wiki for your pages"

→ drop any file into /raw (transcript, pdf, screenshot, meeting notes). type one word: ingest

→ claude writes a wiki page, links it to 5 existing ones, updates CLAUDE.md with any new pattern it caught about how you think

→ never open a blank chat again. every question goes through the vault. every answer cites your own sources with dates and links

5 minutes to wire. runs forever on the laptop already in front of you

the alpha most people miss:

> search your own vault in one line and the answer cites 5 of your own past notes with dates. google cites strangers. your vault cites you

> every ingest adds cross-links to 5 past pages automatically. after 90 days your vault answers questions you forgot you had

> CLAUDE.md learns how you argue, what you change your mind on, what you avoid saying. after month 3 it drafts posts in your voice better than you can at 2am

> flip two flags and it runs on local llama. zero API bill, zero vendor lock, your thinking never leaves the box

> compounds for 10 years. after year 3 your vault knows more about what you believe than you do. year 5 and recruiters start asking you to publish parts of it

the ugly part most will scroll past:

your coworker started this on a saturday in february

by august his tweets landed 4x your engagement on the exact same topics

by october his first draft of any doc was already better than your third

the gap is one 5 minute install and 90 days of ingesting what you already consume for free

你读过的每一篇文章，你听过的每一篇播客，你参加的每一次会议，你拥有的每一条DM线程，你起草的每一条推文，所有这些都可以永远在一行中搜索

今天运行它的人不再打开chatgpt。他们打开自己的搜索栏。他们的搜索栏里有他们11年的思考

堆栈：

→brew 安装黑曜石，mkdir ~/vault，cd ~/vault

→ 在该文件夹中打开 Claude Code，输入“init CLAUDE.md 作为规则，/raw 作为源代码，/wiki 作为您的页面”

→ 将任何文件放入 /raw（记录、pdf、屏幕截图、会议记录）。输入一个词：摄入

→ claude 编写了一个 wiki 页面，将其链接到 5 个现有页面，用它捕获的关于您的想法的任何新模式更新 CLAUDE.md

→ 永远不要再打开空白聊天室。每个问题都会经过保险库。每个答案都引用了您自己的来源，并附有日期和链接

5 分钟即可接线。在您面前的笔记本电脑上永远运行

大多数人怀念的阿尔法：

> 在一行中搜索你自己的金库，答案引用了你自己过去的 5 篇笔记并附有日期。谷歌引用陌生人。你的金库引用了你

> 每次收录都会自动添加到过去 5 个页面的交叉链接。 90 天后，您的金库会回答您忘记的问题

> CLAUDE.md 了解您如何争论、您改变主意以及您避免说什么。第三个月后，它会比你在凌晨 2 点更好地用你的声音起草帖子

> 翻转两个标志，它就在本地美洲驼上运行。零 API 账单、零供应商锁定，您的思维永远不会脱离盒子

> 化合物有效期为 10 年。第三年之后，你的金库比你自己更了解你的信仰。第 5 年，招聘人员开始要求你发布其中的部分内容

丑陋的部分大部分都会滚动过去：

你的同事在二月的一个星期六开始了这个

到 8 月，他的推文使您对同一主题的参与度提高了 4 倍

到十月，他的任何文档的初稿都已经比你的第三稿好

差距是 5 分钟安装和 90 天免费获取已使用的内容

BREAKING: I asked Claude Code to turn my WiFi router into a radar. It worked.

No camera. No extra sensor. Claude wrote the code in 40 minutes. It reads how the WiFi signal bends around bodies and draws them as moving shapes on a map of my apartment.

I ran it at night to test it. Living room: me. Kitchen: empty. Bedroom: a second shape.

I live alone.

I thought it was a bug. I walked to the bedroom. The shape didn’t move. The map showed it standing next to the bed, facing the door.

I turned it off. I still don’t know what the code was reading.

If your router is on right now, it’s already doing half the job.

title:
Great way to think of your next AI use case ⬇️

You ended your work day and you still have items on your to-do list.

Re
title_en:
Great way to think of your next AI use case ⬇️

You ended your work day and you still have items on your to-do list.

Read that list. 

Those are the the problems that AI is still not good enough to solve for, we can't or don't trust it enough to solve for, or may never be good enough to solve for.

"I have to review this email before I send it" - consider that you don't trust AI enough to reason on that issue or it still doesn't quite write like you. Perhaps spend more time on your "write like me" skill or build out another eval for that process to catch the most common or obvious things you're reviewing for. 

"I have to fill this thing out online and it has to be perfect" - then computer use isn't good enough, or you don't know it's good enough. If it makes sense, ask AI to complete the task one-by-one, watch it work, witness its performance. What, if anything, failed? Can you improve it for next time?

"I have to wait for Bobby to respond to my email" - consider additional workflows supporting on team alignment or team handoffs, something that nearly every enterprise I speak with is still struggling with.

Literally just end your work day and look at what is still left. 

That list will tell you what of your own workflows to improve with AI or where you can carve out a business for others with the same lingering list item.

思考下一个人工智能用例的好方法⬇️

您结束了一天的工作，但待办事项清单上仍有项目。

阅读该列表。

这些是人工智能仍然不足以解决的问题，我们不能或不相信它能够解决，或者可能永远不足以解决。

“在发送之前我必须先检查一下这封电子邮件”——考虑到你对人工智能的信任度不够，无法在这个问题上进行推理，或者它的写作方式仍然不太像你。也许花更多的时间在你的“像我一样写作”技能上，或者为这个过程建立另一个评估，以捕捉你正在审查的最常见或最明显的事情。

“我必须在网上填写这个东西，而且它必须是完美的”——那么计算机的使用就不够好，或者你不知道它足够好。如果有意义，请人工智能一项一项地完成任务，观察它的工作，见证它的表现。如果有什么失败的话？下次可以改进一下吗？

“我必须等待 Bobby 回复我的电子邮件”——考虑支持团队协调或团队交接的额外工作流程，这是我接触过的几乎每个企业仍在努力解决的问题。

title:
💸 Update: My total biz expenses have now dropped to just ~$300/mo!

This is to run all my websites/apps serving per year
title_en:
💸 Update: My total biz expenses have now dropped to just ~$300/mo!

This is to run all my websites/apps serving per year:
- 20,000 paying customers
- 252 million visitors
- 2.4 billion requests
- 2.4 petabyte (PB) in bandwidth

(~$8,000/mo if you add the $7,000/mo GPU bill and $800/mo R2 storage I pay for Photo AI, I exclude it above because it's one project that's so much more expensive in size than all the other sites together, but included in the chart below)

Claude Code helped me to find smart ways to save more money, AI is just really really really good at finding cost savings by itself, which is not so great for the economy short-term, but long term it trims all the fat and opens up spending for better investments I think

Anyway here's what it saved me in money, almost $34,000/mo:

- $29,000/mo - switched to better and cheaper video models on Photo AI, video was very expensive and since I didn't update it ever it stayed expensive, also routed some image jobs to Google Cloud where I have some Google Cloud Credits, and also routed some jobs to Sume which sells AI models at market cost, very cool! This made my GPU bill go from $36,000/mo to $7,000/mo

- $3,000/mo - consolidated my servers, cancelled Digital Ocean and Linode and moved everything to Hetzner saving about $3,000/mo

- $1100/mo - analyzed my Backblaze B2 server backups, I had infinite versioning and lifecycle policies, that's reduced now to 30 days, this literally pushed the bill from $1,200/mo to $26/mo, about 50x cheaper! I had essentially versions of files for all my servers for over a decade, crazy!

- $400/mo - similarly added Lifecycle Policies to my Cloudflare R2 bucket for Photo AI, pics are automatically put in cheaper Infrequent Access after 90 days, there was years of photos in there so this reduced the R2 bill from $1,200/mo to $800/mo

- $118/mo - Claude analyzed all my Cloudflare Domain registrations, lots of domains I didn't use and didn't make sense to keep paying for, lots of things that also don't really make sense anymore in a post-AGI world, renewals for .io TLD are now $50/year which adds up fast!

- $100/mo - Claude also analyzed my Claude subscription (yes!) and discovered I don't even use the Max 20x plan limits, so I downgraded from $200/mo to $100/mo

Even including Photo AI, I have now cut my costs by 90% from last year, getting me close to my biz expenses amount from a decade ago when I started building things

Costs slowly creep up over the years and you don't realize all the things you're spending on but AI is nice to help you figure all that out (also in your personal life!)

Claude Code 帮助我找到了节省更多钱的明智方法，人工智能本身真的非常非常擅长节省成本，这对短期经济来说并不是那么好，但从长远来看，它会削减所有的脂肪并为更好的投资打开支出

不管怎样，这就是它为我节省的钱，大约 34,000 美元/月：

- 29,000 美元/月 - 在 Photo AI 上切换到更好、更便宜的视频模型，视频非常昂贵，因为我没有更新它，所以它仍然很昂贵，还将一些图像作业路由到 Google Cloud，在那里我有一些 Google Cloud Credits，并且还将一些作业路由到 Sume，它以市场成本销售 AI 模型，非常酷！这使得我的 GPU 账单从 36,000 美元/月增加到 7,000 美元/月

- 每月 3,000 美元 - 整合了我的服务器，取消了 Digital Ocean 和 Linode，并将所有内容转移到 Hetzner，每月节省了约 3,000 美元

多年来，成本慢慢上升，你并没有意识到你花在了所有的事情上，但人工智能可以很好地帮助你弄清楚所有这些（也在你的个人生活中！）

Claude Code 帮助我找到了节省更多钱的明智方法，人工智能本身真的非常非常擅长节省成本，这对短期经济来说并不是那么好，但从长远来看，它会削减所有的脂肪并为更好的投资打开支出

不管怎样，这就是它为我节省的钱，大约 34,000 美元/月：

- 29,000 美元/月 - 在 Photo AI 上切换到更好、更便宜的视频模型，视频非常昂贵，因为我没有更新它，所以它仍然很昂贵，还将一些图像作业路由到 Google Cloud，在那里我有一些 Google Cloud Credits，并且还将一些作业路由到 Sume，它以市场成本销售 AI 模型，非常酷！这使得我的 GPU 账单从 36,000 美元/月增加到 7,000 美元/月

- 每月 3,000 美元 - 整合了我的服务器，取消了 Digital Ocean 和 Linode，并将所有内容转移到 Hetzner，每月节省了约 3,000 美元

- 1100 美元/月 - 分析了我的 Backblaze B2 服务器备份，我有无限的版本控制和生命周期策略，现在减少到 30 天，这实际上将账单从 1,200 美元/月推至 26 美元/月，便宜了大约 50 倍！十多年来，我的所有服务器基本上都有文件版本，太疯狂了！

- 400 美元/月 - 同样在我的 Cloudflare R2 存储桶中添加用于照片 AI 的生命周期策略，90 天后图片会自动放入更便宜的不频繁访问中，那里有多年的照片，因此这将 R2 费用从 1,200 美元/月减少到 800 美元/月

- 118 美元/月 - Claude 分析了我所有的 Cloudflare 域名注册，很多域名我没有使用过，也没有必要继续付费，很多东西在后 AGI 世界中也不再有意义，.io TLD 的续订现在是 50 美元/年，加起来很快！

- 100 美元/月 - Claude 还分析了我的 Claude 订阅（是的！），发现我什至没有使用 Max 20x 计划限制，因此我从 200 美元/月降级至 100 美元/月

即使包括 Photo AI，我现在也比去年削减了 90% 的成本，这让我接近十年前开始构建产品时的业务支出金额

多年来，成本慢慢上升，你并没有意识到你花在了所有的事情上，但人工智能可以很好地帮助你弄清楚所有这些（也在你的个人生活中！）

title:
Every serious PE-backed company has AI agents now.

Very few have one running anywhere but on somebody’s laptop.

I was
title_en:
Every serious PE-backed company has AI agents now.

Very few have one running anywhere but on somebody’s laptop.

I was speaking to a relatively tech-forward operator at a distributor. Smart team, AI licenses for everyone, two or three people sharp enough to start building.

“We’ve built some great stuff. I just wouldn’t put any of it in front of a customer.”

His team has the same thing in common with almost every PE portco I talk to.

They have a pile of agents:

→ A pricing tool someone built in Claude Code.
→ A folder of “skills”.
→ A prototype vibe coded by a contractor.
→ A daily briefing assistant for the CEO.

They have budget and a sponsor too. Most of them even have urgency.

But every agent still lives on the laptop of whoever built it.

That's the pattern in every case: leadership treats agents as something the builder should maintain “on the side.”

An EA runs the CEO’s calendar and also babysits five bots.

This operator runs finance & ops and “owns” the pricing tool he built in Claude Code.

A contractor vibe codes a prototype, and nobody can say what it would take to keep it running once his contract ends.

I asked one PE partner how many of his portfolio companies have an agent hosted somewhere real. "One, maybe."

A laptop isn’t production, and "on the side" isn’t ownership.

You either give the agent a home (hosted, with an owner, access controls, monitoring, and a spend cap), turn it into a script, or kill it.

Most leadership teams just leave it on a laptop and call it a pilot.
title_zh:
现在，每家严肃的私募股权投资公司都拥有人工智能代理。

除了在某人的笔记本电脑上运行之外，很少有人在任何地方运行。

我正在与一家分销商的一位技术相对先进的操作员交谈。聪明的团队，每个人都有人工智能许可证，两三个人足够敏锐就可以开始构建。
full_text_en:
Every serious PE-backed company has AI agents now.

Very few have one running anywhere but on somebody’s laptop.

I was speaking to a relatively tech-forward operator at a distributor. Smart team, AI licenses for everyone, two or three people sharp enough to start building.

“We’ve built some great stuff. I just wouldn’t put any of it in front of a customer.”

His team has the same thing in common with almost every PE portco I talk to.

They have a pile of agents:

→ A pricing tool someone built in Claude Code.
→ A folder of “skills”.
→ A prototype vibe coded by a contractor.
→ A daily briefing assistant for the CEO.

They have budget and a sponsor too. Most of them even have urgency.

But every agent still lives on the laptop of whoever built it.

That's the pattern in every case: leadership treats agents as something the builder should maintain “on the side.”

An EA runs the CEO’s calendar and also babysits five bots.

This operator runs finance & ops and “owns” the pricing tool he built in Claude Code.

A contractor vibe codes a prototype, and nobody can say what it would take to keep it running once his contract ends.

I asked one PE partner how many of his portfolio companies have an agent hosted somewhere real. "One, maybe."

A laptop isn’t production, and "on the side" isn’t ownership.

You either give the agent a home (hosted, with an owner, access controls, monitoring, and a spend cap), turn it into a script, or kill it.

Most leadership teams just leave it on a laptop and call it a pilot.
full_text_zh:
现在，每家严肃的私募股权投资公司都拥有人工智能代理。

除了在某人的笔记本电脑上运行之外，很少有人在任何地方运行。

我正在与一家分销商的一位技术相对先进的操作员交谈。聪明的团队，每个人都有人工智能许可证，两三个人足够敏锐就可以开始构建。

“我们已经构建了一些很棒的东西。我只是不会把它们放在客户面前。”

他的团队与我交谈过的几乎所有 PE Portco 都有相同的共同点。

他们有一堆代理：

→ 有人用 Claude Code 构建的定价工具。
→ “技能”文件夹。
→ 由承包商编码的原型氛围。
→ 首席执行官的每日简报助理。

他们也有预算和赞助商。他们中的大多数人甚至都有紧迫感。

但每个特工仍然依赖于建造它的人的笔记本电脑。

这就是每种情况下的模式：领导层将代理视为建筑商应该“站在一边”维护的东西。

EA 负责管理 CEO 的日历，并照顾五个机器人。

该运营商负责财务和运营，并“拥有”他在 Claude Code 中构建的定价工具。

承包商氛围对原型进行了编码，没有人能说出在合同结束后如何才能使其保持运行。

我问一位私募股权合伙人，他的投资组合公司中有多少家在真实的地方设有代理人。 “一个，也许吧。”

笔记本电脑不是生产产品，“二手”也不是所有权。

您要么给代理一个家（托管，有所有者、访问控制、监控和支出上限），要么将其变成脚本，要么杀死它。

大多数领导团队只是将其放在笔记本电脑上并称之为试点。

title_en:
I made an AI agent plan a $3,600 Greece trip for two.

Then asked it to plan another trip to Portugal.

Guess how much of the workflow I had to rebuild?

ZERO.

I used Teamily AI's team agents to handle the research and destination comparisons while my teammate and I reviewed the options.

It reminded me of this line from Summer's piece:

"Humans + Agents. One Team."

Here's what I did:

→ Created a Travel Research Agent
→ Built a Loop with the agent, me, and my teammate
→ Asked it to research a 5-day Greece trip and rank the best options
→ Reviewed the shortlist together in the group

Then reused the SAME Loop for Portugal.

All I had to do was change the trip requirements and run it again.

No repeating instructions or setting up everyone's roles twice.

I'd much rather have the agent do the research and leave the actual decisions to us.

This is how I built and ran it in Teamily AI: 👇

title: Even in bypass permissions mode, Claude Code still asks before a few especially risky rm commands. That’s intentional, b
title_en:
Even in bypass permissions mode, Claude Code still asks before a few especially risky rm commands. That’s intentional, but if you’re in a throwaway container and are okay with those running without asking, you can now set CLAUDE_CODE_EVEN_MORE_DANGEROUSLY_SKIP_PERMISSIONS=1.

And shell commands that hit their timeout now keep running in the background instead of getting cut off, so a long build or test suite isn’t killed halfway.
title_zh: 即使在绕过权限模式下，Claude Code 仍然会在一些特别危险的 rm 命令之前询问。这是故意的，但如果您位于一次性容器中并且无需询问就可以运行这些容器，那么您现在可以设置 CLAUDE_CODE_EVEN_MORE_DANGEROUS
full_text_en:
Even in bypass permissions mode, Claude Code still asks before a few especially risky rm commands. That’s intentional, but if you’re in a throwaway container and are okay with those running without asking, you can now set CLAUDE_CODE_EVEN_MORE_DANGEROUSLY_SKIP_PERMISSIONS=1.

And shell commands that hit their timeout now keep running in the background instead of getting cut off, so a long build or test suite isn’t killed halfway.
full_text_zh:
即使在绕过权限模式下，Claude Code 仍然会在一些特别危险的 rm 命令之前询问。这是故意的，但如果您位于一次性容器中并且无需询问就可以运行这些容器，那么您现在可以设置 CLAUDE_CODE_EVEN_MORE_DANGEROUSLY_SKIP_PERMISSIONS=1。

现在，遇到超时的 shell 命令会继续在后台运行，而不是被切断，因此较长的构建或测试套件不会中途被终止。

title_en:
You also get a bit more control over Claude's effort.

Typing ultrathink in a message now bumps effort to xhigh for just that one turn, so you can think harder on one problem without changing your setting for the whole session.

You can now also tell Claude which effort level to run a subagent at. If your session is on high but you want the subagents for a task on medium, just ask! 

And /usage in the CLI now tells you in plain words what's using up your limits. If there's a quick fix, you can press f to apply it right there.

现在，在消息中输入 ultrathink 会将这一回合的努力提升至 xhigh，因此您可以更加努力地思考一个问题，而无需更改整个会话的设置。

您现在还可以告诉 Claude 运行子代理的工作量级别。如果您的会话级别较高，但您希望子代理执行中等级别的任务，请直接询问！

CLI 中的 /usage 现在可以用简单的语言告诉您什么耗尽了您的限制。如果有快速修复方法，您可以按 f 立即应用它。
